And it comes with a spicy chili sauce that perfectly enhances the savory beef filling.
perfect_for_tags: Chinese

review: Bird’s Nest In Lakeview is a bar with great chicken wings. Each wing is meaty and juicy, and has wonderfully crunchy bits. Order them with the Birds Nest hot sauce (which is perfectly peppery), and you have a perfect drinking snack.
perfect_for_tags: Bar Food

review: Output is a sports bar in West Town with has great chicken wings. Instead of the typical variations you get at most bars, they have flavors like savory lemon pepper and roasted garlic BBQ. They’re so delicious on their own that extra dipping sauces are unnecessary. Come here to watch sports, drink beer, and eat as many wings as you can.
perfect_for_tags: Bar Food

review: This fried chicken spot has blessed the homes of Chicagoans with great smells and delicious food since 1963. Historically in competition with Harold’s (another local chain) Uncle Remus has its own unique style. The chicken is double-coated with their seasoned batter, deep-fried to crunchy perfection, and then dressed with their sweet and tangy mild sauce.
perfect_for_tags: Southern, Fried Chicken

review: You come to Woodies for the chicken wings. They're are air-dried, slow-smoked, and double-fried. That careful preparation makes them very tasty, but it’s their long list of delicious sauces that sets Woodies apart. You’ll find flavors like cheesy garlic, Nashville hot, Chimichurri, or Korean BBQ, and you can order them bone-in, grilled, or boneless.
perfect_for_tags: American, Bar Food

review: This Pilsen bakery offers more than 10 vegan options, many of which are classic pan dulce or “sweetbreads.” While you may instantly recognize the pastel pink or cocoa-dusted conchas, Nuevo Leon has other classics you should try, starting with the abanico, or fan, made of palotiado, a flaky Mexican pastry. Sweet with a buttery crust, these are perfect for dipping into coffee. Another coffee-friendly treat is the marranito, a molasses “polvorón” or shortbread cookie shaped like a pig - and yes, much like animal crackers, these are still vegan despite their resemblance to the real thing. This cookie is a comforting blend of spicy and sweet, and the top is crackly in the most satisfying way. The cutest part? They mark the cookie with a little “v” so you know it’s vegan-friendly.
perfect_for_tags: Literally Everyone, Vegans, Mexican, Dessert

review: If you want to impress vegans and omnivorous friends alike, head over to one of West Town Bakery’s many locations because they have something that will please just about anyone. This Chicago institution serves cakes, scones, muffins, donuts, and about a hundred other things, all of which they make from scratch in their bakery. If you’re looking for a morning treat, you can’t beat their vegan chocolate or banana nut muffins. Alternatively, West Town Bakery is one of the best places to find vegan cupcakes. Theirs are smooth without being too oily, which is sometimes insurmountable in vegan baking, given that oil often replaces eggs. While their flagship location is on Chicago Avenue in West Town, you can also find them in Wrigleyville. Their River North location in the Acme Hotel is temporarily closed, but they expect to open back up in the next few months.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Lunch, Vegans, Sandwiches, Dessert

review: If you recognize the play on words there, this bakery is for you. The purveyor of “sweet treats for the misfit soul” aims to make the most indulgent and delicious vegan desserts imaginable. Once a steadily growing vegan pop-up, Pie, Pie, My Darling now has a storefront bakery located in Humboldt Park. Every weekend after Pie Pie My Darling’s initial opening in 2019, a line of people formed down Chicago Ave waiting to get their hands on cosmic brownies, cookies, pies, and more. Cake jars - mason jars with layers of buttercream and cake pieces that didn’t make the final cut - are also a fan favorite for being downright delicious while cutting down food waste. Since the pandemic, they’ve switched to a pre-order-only system. Ordering from your couch may be more convenient than standing in line for an hour, but items sell out in minutes, so be prepared to camp in front of your laptop with your credit card number memorized.
perfect_for_tags: Birthdays, Literally Everyone, Vegans, Dessert, Bakery/Cafe

review: They call themselves the best churro in the Midwest, and we can’t disagree with the people at Don Churro. As you would expect from the name, they specialize in churros, but what they lack in variety they make up for in perfect execution. Their vegan churro options are exceptional, having a standard churro and two filled varieties. The strawberry and guava-filled churros are fruity and sweet without overwhelming the already sugary pastry dough, which we think is worthy of a national holiday. With three churros to choose from, you might as well snag all three.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Literally Everyone, Vegans, Mexican, Dessert
full_address: 1626 S Blue Island Ave, Chicago, IL 60608

review: This gluten-free bakery in Andersonville has every sweet you could ever want. Plus, many of their options happen to be vegan as well. You'll see their packaged pastries for sale all over Chicago, but we recommend ordering some of their specialties for pick up at their storefront, where they have even more options. Their oatmeal cream pie is a decadent twist on a familiar Little Debbie favorite, while the ginger molasses cookie is the perfect blend of sweet and spicy. Since the start of the pandemic, Defloured has instituted a very efficient pick-up system, in which you must order at least 24 hours in advance and retrieve your goodies at their storefront at your designated time.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Gluten-Free Options, Vegans, Dessert, Bakery/Cafe

review: Of all the vegan bakeries in Chicago, Bot Bakery might have the best variety while also being completely gluten-free. They do special order cakes, cupcakes, and cookies in addition to their storefront offerings, which they always keep interesting. Their sourdough cinnamon rolls are an inventive take on a classic, with the sourdough lending the traditionally sweet bread a slight tang. And their peanut butter sandwich cookies are also a must-try, especially if you grew up loving Nutter Butters. Because of COVID-19, they are currently pre-order only, and they require at least a four-day notice, but the wait is totally worth it.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Gluten-Free Options, Literally Everyone, Vegans, Dessert, Bakery/Cafe
full_address: 7100 S South Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60649

review: Thankfully, it’s much easier to find a vegan cake around town now than it was a few years ago - even ones made of vegan ice cream. You can customize your very own cake, or you can order a dozen vegan chocolate chip cookies if you're looking for something simpler. Our recommendation? Their ginger-rum ice cream sandwich consists of a unique, tropical homemade ice cream between two chewy oatmeal cookies, which somehow channels both grandma's house and the beach. The light rum flavor from the ice cream is the closest you can get to vacation via cookie, so it checks all our boxes. The only catch is that Bartleby's is pre-order only, and their items come in multiples, making them ideal for sharing (or not).
perfect_for_tags: Birthdays, Literally Everyone, Vegans, Ice Cream, Dessert

review: We simply can’t walk down Division Street in Wicker Park without stopping to look at the cakes on display at Alliance Bakery’s storefront. But they have more than cakes, they also offer breakfast pastries, cupcakes, and cookies. Of all their vegan options, Alliance’s peanut-butter chocolate vegan cupcake steals the show. The thick swirl of salty and sweet peanut butter buttercream offsets the bittersweet chocolate base. Dusted with fine cocoa powder, it’s a fancy cupcake that actually delivers on flavor, too. Unfortunately, Alliance only has one vegan cupcake flavor, but here’s to hoping they expand soon.
perfect_for_tags: Literally Everyone, Vegans, Dessert, Bakery/Cafe

review: Uncle Joe’s Hyde Park serves quintessential Jamaican food. They do everything - oxtails, jerk catfish, curry shrimp, and more, really well. They simply have the various Jamaican flavor profiles down. If you’re looking for a dish to start with, try the $15 jerk chicken wing dinner that comes with two sides or the $20 combo plate that includes two types of meat and plantains, rice and peas, jerk sauce, and bread.
perfect_for_tags: Caribbean
full_address: 1461 E Hyde Park Blvd, Chicago, IL 60615

review: Not only does Tropic Island in Chatham have tasty jerk, but you get an impressive amount of food for the price. It's $12.50 for a white meat jerk dinner with three sides. Go with rice and peas, plantain, and macaroni and cheese, but you can choose between those or five other sides that they offer. Also good to know is that they have locations in Calumet City and Muenster, Indiana.
perfect_for_tags: Caribbean

review: It’s all about the oxtails in Jamaican cooking, and Aunty Joy’s in Edgewater doesn’t disappoint. The oxtails are succulent and, even better, you can choose between a small or a large order in addition to a choice of two sides, like steamed cabbage or rice and peas.)
perfect_for_tags: Caribbean

review: Jerk Taco Man Caribbean BBQ restaurant has built quite the following around their fantastic jerk chicken tacos. They’re huge, coming in at half a pound each, topped with cheese, cilantro, and onion on a flour tortilla. Their menu is huge too, offering jerk veggie tacos, jerk pasta, and of course, jerk chicken. Grab a jerk taco or any of their other offerings at either their Garfield Park or Park Manor locations.
perfect_for_tags: Caribbean

review: Birrieria El Texcal is a favorite in Albany Park. The birria is buttery from hours of slow roasting, and the hefty birria tacos are full of meat. Options include goat or lamb, your choice of either corn or flour tortillas, and each comes with a side of rice and beans.  Stop by, or call in your order early - they open at 10am.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Mexican, Tacos

review: Some are new to this, but Birrieria Ocotlan is true to this. They’ve been serving incredible birria (and now quesabirria tacos) since 1978. It’s a family recipe, and they like to keep things traditional with choices including beef and goat tacos. A “Combo Quesatacos″ includes three quesabirria tacos, beans, rice, a pop (yes, pop, not soda), and of course, a side of consomé.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Mexican, Tacos

review: Tacotlan in Hermosa really does birria, and they have a whole separate menu to prove it. That menu includes birria ramen, and even bizza (birria pizza). According to co-owner Jessica Perjes (and her father and co-owner Everado Macias), Tacotlan is one of the first restaurants to introduce quesabirria to Chicago, and the proof is in their delicious tacos. Theirs oozes chihuahua cheese, and if the tacos weren’t great enough, the side of consomé could be a dish by itself.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Serious Take-Out Operation, Mexican, Tacos

review: El Asador is a lively Mexican restaurant in Gage Park. And one of our favorite things to order here is their beef quesabirria. It's a new offering and can be ordered at both their 47th and 51st location. You can get the three or four taco quesabirria dinner - it comes with rice and beans, along with a side of cilantro, onion, and the consomé.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Mexican, Tacos

review: Tata’s Tacos in Portage Park describes their au-jus consommé as “down and dirty,” and we're not ashamed to admit that’s how we looked after we finished eating their birria tacos. Tata’s sears their tortillas in the consommé, which gives the tacos an extra flavor boost. In addition to the cheesy birria, they offer at least a dozen types of tacos, including The Tux, a seared scallop and ribeye taco, and the Jibarito which is served on a plantain tortilla.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Mexican, Tacos
full_address: 4929 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60641

review: After a fire closed their Pilsen restaurant last summer, Jarabe is now operating out of Dr. Murphy’s Food Hall. But you’ll still find wine and cream-colored heirloom corn lining the counter, which is used to make masa for their hand-pressed tortillas. The quesabirria tacos are rich, and their escabeche adds a brightly flavored crunch. Do yourself a favor and grab a few of their cochinita pibil tacos and a cucumber agua fresca while you’re here, too. You’ll be happy you did.
perfect_for_tags: Mexican, Tacos

review: Anyone who spent time in their 20s at a bar in Chicago has probably gotten a tamale from The Tamale Guy (even if they don’t remember it). Well Claudio Velez, the actual Tamale Guy, finally opened up his own physical restaurant. And it turns out that his perfectly fluffy tamales are better than ever. Plus, now he also has birria down to a science, made with oxtail, beef cheek, and chuck roast. There's crispy char on both the birria and chihuahua cheese, and you should consider yourself lucky if you can get one before they run out.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Mexican

review: Minahasa started as a pop-up run by the chef and his mother (Mama Betty), and is now operating out of Revival Food Hall in the Loop. This Indonesian restaurant has delicious things like soto ayam, beef rendang, and sambal chicken wings, along with ube cookies and balapis. And while the food hall is open for indoor dining, you can still get Minahasa for takeout and delivery.
perfect_for_tags: Indonesian

review: Good Ambler is a bakery in the West Loop, and we've yet to find something here that's not absolutely delicious. You’ll find everything from macarons to alfajores, petit gateau, pastries, and handmade chocolates. Stop in for a cup of coffee, and potentially pick up way more pastries than one person needs.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Bakery/Cafe

review: This brand new Peranakan spot is from the owners of Serai in Logan Square. Unlike Serai, which is casual and more of a carryout operation, Kapitan is located in Lincoln Park and designed to be a sit-down restaurant. Kapitan serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner all-day, with dishes like pie tee, chee cheong fun, a whole roasted Hainanese chicken, and kuih that changes every week.
perfect_for_tags: Indonesian

review: The original Mary’s has been in Garfield Park since 1968, and this is their carryout and delivery-only location operating out of a shared kitchen space in Humboldt Park. The menu is the same as their original location, with things like rib tips, fried catfish, wings, and burgers.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, BBQ

review: Retreat is a long-term pop-up (the plan is for it to last a year) happening at the Currency Exchange Cafe in Garfield Park. It’s a spot for BIPOC creatives to showcase their food (as well as art and music), with a rotating list of chefs and artists.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Coffee & A Light Bite, Bakery/Cafe

review: This is a new carryout and delivery-only spot operating out of The Hatchery - a restaurant incubator in Garfield Park. And Empanada Mama focuses on (you guessed it) empanadas, along with bites like shrimp ceviche and Puerto Rican rice.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Latin

review: This takeout-only spot in Avondale specializes in Japanese curry. The menu has things like tonkatsu kare, a shaved beef udon curry, and waffle fries (yes, topped with curry). Both the chicken and pork are incredibly juicy, the handmade noodles are wonderfully chewy, and we’re glad the rich curry is covering everything since it's delicious.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Japanese

review: There are a lot of great West African restaurants in Uptown, and Palace Gate Ghanaian Restaurant is one of our favorites. There are a lot of different stews, rice, and starches that making up the menu, and we really like the meat and jollof plate. It’s a heaping serving of spicy, fragrant rice, tender stewed beef, and ripe, roasted plantain.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Ghanaian

review: This West Loop spot is a barbershop in the daytime, but at night, Blind Barber turns into a bar. And this year, this bar/barbershop hybrid has an outdoor patio so you (and your great haircut) can drink outside.
perfect_for_tags: Drinking Good Cocktails, Bar Food

review: There is nothing - we repeat nothing - not to love about D&D’s donuts in Ashburn. Not only are the donuts fantastic, but this place is incredibly likable - you get handed a donut hole to try when you walk-in and they give away free (and actually delicious) giant donuts to any kid that brings in their report card. Everything is great - from the glazed and blueberry to the apple fritters that are about 10 inches across, three inches thick, and a literal wonderland of textures. In conclusion, cancel out the rest of your day and dedicate it to this donut.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Bakery/Cafe

review: If you haven’t had the ribs from Full Slab in Stony Island, you need to cancel whatever you originally planned on doing today to correct this. The ribs are tender and chewy, have a satisfyingly charred bark, and are lacquered with their sweet, slightly spicy, Chicago sauce. Also, for god’s sake, get the baked beans. They’re tangy, sweet, and will change your life.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, BBQ
full_address: 8340 S Stony Island Ave, Chicago, IL 60617

review: If donut shops had coaching trees, then Old Fashioned Donuts would be Bill Parcells. This Roseland spot has been around for over 40 years, and people who have worked here (like the owners of D&D’s for example) have gone on to open their own successful donut shops. This place started the giant donut trend, but if you’re looking for a regulation-sized donut, their yeasted glazed is fantastic.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Bakery/Cafe

review: Chicago has a strong pizza identity. We claim two styles as “ours″ (deep dish and tavern) and will ruin a perfectly nice evening debating the best of each. But unlike some of our friends in New York, our city supports all kinds of pizza—even Bob’s, whose Pilsen-style just got approved by the Chicago Department of Pizza Style Regulation and Licensing.  Recently, we’ve seen a bunch of new places making Sicilian-style—and the best of them is Pizza Friendly Pizza. In fact, this little spot in Ukrainian Village is making some of our favorite pizza in Chicago, period. We’re really not surprised the pies here are excellent - they come from the chef of Oriole, one of the best tasting-menu restaurants in the city. But Pizza Friendly Pizza is the opposite of fine dining. It’s a carryout-window in an alley, and you can either get the food to-go, sit in their little dining room, or eat on their small patio next to some garbage cans. The last of which you won’t even notice are there because the pizza is so f*cking good.  The excellent Sicilian pan-style pizza comes by the slice, or you can pre-order a full pie. The thick crust is incredibly light and airy with a slight sourdough-y flavor, and the tomato sauce is rich and spicy. The short menu has a few varieties available, like the charred pepperoni (that are perfect little grease cups) and one of our favorite, the Ruben’s Special, which is topped with sausage and a delicious housemade giardiniera. There are also a few sandwiches and salads, both of which are good, but shame on you if you come here and don’t order any pizza. Which you might want to do ahead of time, because this place regularly sells out. But don’t get too discouraged if they’re sold out online, they usually still have slices available. Since our lust for pizza is never sated, there will always be more new spots opening up in Chicago. And like a pizza Ellis Island, we’ll continue to welcome them with open arms. But for now, we’re happy to just keep ordering from Pizza Friendly Pizza.
food_rundown:
Pepperoni Pizza

Some people like large pepperoni that drape over the slice like bed sheets, but not us. Luckily Pizza Friendly Pizza has the kind of little burnt pepperoni cups that we love. Their pepperoni slice is also topped with burrata and basil.


Ruben’s Special

This isn’t a Rueben pizza. We repeat, it’s NOT a Rueben pizza. It’s _Ruben’s_ pizza, and whoever they are they’re clearly obsessed with delicious giardiniera. It’s perfectly pickled and spicy, so it doesn’t overwhelm the flavor of the sausage, and finely chopped so it’s distributed perfectly on the pizza. If you like giardiniera even a little, this slice is a must-order.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Pizza

review: Fry The Coop started in the suburbs, and unlike your cousin, this is a suburban import we enjoy. Their specialty is Nashville hot chicken and it is seriously hot. There are six heat levels to choose from (ranging from “country” to ‘insanity”) and we suggest finding a designated driver if you order anything above “hot.” If you really appreciate and seek out spicy, juicy chicken, you’ll love this place.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Fried Chicken

review: The fried chicken here is find here is simple and delicious. And what makes Crazy Bird in West Town really stand out is the excellent sides, and perfectly proportioned sandwiches. The lightly-breaded crispy chicken has the size and shape of a pounded cutlet. It’s still really juicy, but also thin enough to create an enjoyable (and manageable) bread-to-meat bite ratio.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Sandwiches

review: This is a fantastic sandwich shop. For example, the Cambodian fried chicken sandwich is a straight-up flavor parade. The thigh is brined with things like lemongrass, garlic, galangal, and turmeric, tossed in fish sauce, and then fried in rice flour. After that, it’s topped with sweet and spicy pickled papaya and put inside a brioche bun.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Sandwiches, Southeast Asian

review: Ms. T’s makes excellent fried chicken - it’s light and crispy. We’re also big fans of the sandwich, made with two tenders on a hamburger bun and your choice of sauce - and you’re going to want the gold sauce. And if you don’t order a deep-fried, butter-infused biscuit while you’re here, we feel sorry for you.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Southern

review: This spot in University Village has incredibly creamy soft serve, ice cream, melon pan ice cream sandwiches, and boba tea. The flavors change, but you’ll find not-too-sweet varieties like taro, red bean, sesame, milk tea, and earl grey. And one of our favorite things here is the messy boba - your choice of soft serve topped with boba in a cup.
perfect_for_tags: Ice Cream

review: We’re big fans of this little counter-service Indian spot. The menu is short - they have some build-your-own rice bowls and wraps (with chicken or paneer and tikka sauce). But the best things at Moti are their snacks, particularly the bhel, samosas, and the pani puri. Everything is nicely spicy and perfect for a quick, affordable meal before you decide to go spend $80 on a pair of socks.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Indian, Nepali

review: This coffee shop doubles as a bookstore, one of those ancient places that existed back before Kindles. Build Coffee is located in the Experimental Station in Woodlawn, and being here feels a lot like working in your living room, but with better coffee and fewer cats trying to lay on your laptop. Come for lattes and wifi, and stay to finally finish reading that used copy of On The Road.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Bakery/Cafe

review: We’re big fans of Hexe, a large, industrial-feeling coffee shop located in a section of Roscoe Village filled with office buildings instead of used record shops and brunch places. There’s nothing this place doesn’t do well - along with great coffee and a ton of space to work, Hexe also has outstanding pastries, friendly staff, a fantastic patio, and serves alcohol. Come for work during the day, then stay and meet friends here for drinks at night. Honestly, you might as well sleep here while you’re at it.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Bakery/Cafe

review: When you just need a comfortable place to work for a few hours, Kusanya in Englewood has you covered. This place wants you to sit and stay a while - it literally says so on its website. It’s a pretty standard cafe set-up, with lots of little tables and WiFi, and all the food costs between $2-$5 - dishes like baked oatmeal, grits (you choose either sweet or savory), and the Tuna Turner sandwich, which is just fun to say. And if you do end up staying all-day, they frequently host community events (like poetry and author readings) in the evening.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Walk-Ins, Bakery/Cafe

review: This Chinese spot in Bucktown is from one of our favorite restaurants in Chicago - Giant. And Chef’s Special Cocktail Bar is just as much a very good Chinese restaurant as it is a bar. It’s loud and crowded, and the large space is full of people who are clearly having a good time. The food menu is long, and you’ll find tasty versions of everything from hand-pulled dan dan noodles to shrimp toast to sweet and sour chicken. Most dishes are between $10-$12, and the cocktail list has affordable drinks like the $8 Manager’s Special (whiskey and cherry soda). Just know this place is busy so plan on waiting a while for a seat at the bar (which is first come first served) and definitely make reservations if you want to eat at a table.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Drinking Good Cocktails, Eating At The Bar, Late Night Eats, Small Plates, Chinese

review: Ravenswood and North Center aren’t suffering from a shortage of breakfast spots, but we’re really glad Lizzy J’s (located right on the border) arrived on the scene. This casual breakfast spot has a short, yet delicious soul food menu. You’ll find dishes like chicken and a sweet potato waffle (your choice of light or dark meat), breakfast bowls made with creamy grits, and peaches and cream french toast. Just know this place only has 10 tables, so it’s a good idea to check the waitlist online before heading over.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, American, Southern

review: If you’ve lived in Chicago for any stretch of time, you’ve probably been to El Mariachi in Lakeview. The large back patio is a popular spot for group get-togethers, specifically the ones that involve day drinking. While the OK Mexican food here isn’t going to win any awards (the menu has standards like breakfast burritos and tequila french toast), nothing costs over $10.99. So, honestly, you really can’t afford to not come here.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Brunch, Day Drinking, Mexican

review: Hutch in Andersonville is an all-day spot that offers bottomless brunch every day. This is good news if you don’t work Monday-Friday, or have any job at all. As far as the food goes, you’ll find typical New American dishes like burgers, flatbreads, and salads. The two-level space is large and has lots of big windows for people with vitamin D deficiencies.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, American

review: The only thing that makes Fremont, a club/restaurant in River North even more ridiculously excessive is the bottomless brunch buffet. That’s what you’ll find here, along with a DJ, donut wall, and a retractable roof. Basically, when none of your friends can get their sh*t together for long enough to plan a trip to Vegas, this is your next best option.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Breakfast, Brunch, Dancing, American

review: Things are usually off to a good start at a restaurant when the server puts (free) fresh bread down in front of you. That’s the case at Cafe Istanbul, an upscale Mediterranean restaurant in Wicker Park where most things carb-adjacent are made in-house - lahmacun, pita, even the rigatoni with veal sausage. But the main thing you should focus on here are the meats. The best way to do this is by ordering the mix grill that has a bit of everything, including doner, chicken, beef, shrimp, and lamb kebabs with fluffy basmati rice. The space is loud (the kitchen is semi-open, and there’s a TV in the dining room), but white tablecloths and the full bar make it feel nice enough for a celebratory group dinner.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Dinner with the Parents, Vegetarians, Mediterranean, Turkish

review: Andersonville has a lot of great lunch options, and Middle East Bakery is one you should know about. They’ve got excellent hummus and shawarma, and unlike Taste of Lebanon (another great shawarma option across the street) they’re not just cash-only. When you’re done eating, check out the attached grocery store to take some pita home with you.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Dining Solo, Lunch, Vegetarians, Middle Eastern

review: La Unica is a grocery store in Edgewater that also has a great little Latin American restaurant inside. That means when you’re here you can eat an excellent Cubano with sweet plantains for lunch, and then pick up ingredients to make dinner.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Kids, Lunch, Latin, Mexican

review: Thalia Hall feels like it’s on a slow march to take over the city. In addition to being a great concert venue, the complex has restaurants, bars, and now Paulette’s - a market with groceries and grab-and-go food. If Dusek’s is your spot for a late night meal after the show, and Tack Room is for post-dinner drinks, then Paulette’s is the place you go the morning after for a breakfast sandwich to bring you back to life.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Lunch, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Sandwiches

review: If you’d only seen the CTA ads for Foxtrot Market, you’d probably think it was just one of 17 apps you can use to get a six pack and toilet paper delivered to your apartment. That’s true, but they're also shops with upscale groceries, booze, and $30 candles. The one in Old Town serves breakfast all-day too, with things like bagel sandwiches and spicy chicken biscuits. The food probably won’t blow your mind, but it’s ideal when you need a quick bite while picking up a pint of Jeni’s, a bottle of Chardonnay, and compostable garbage bags.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Coffee & A Light Bite, Delivery, Bakery/Cafe

review: Eataly is a massive, busy Italian market with multiple restaurants and bars inside. It can feel like it’s mainly for tourists, but there are some great reasons for anyone in the area to come, like sandwiches, seafood or a bottle of $86 imported balsamic that you can’t find at your local grocery store.
perfect_for_tags: Dining Solo, Drinks & A Light Bite, Impressing Out of Towners, People Watching, Italian

review: This small cocktail bar in Albany Park  has a lot going on, and we like it. There’s a long drink menu of classic cocktails, signature drinks, beer, and wine, fancy bar snacks like chicken liver pate, and live DJs on the weekend. It’s a great spot for an early-in-the-game date where you’re not sure if you’ll want to leave after the first drink or stick around for food.
perfect_for_tags: Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinks & A Light Bite, Eating At The Bar, First/Early in the Game Dates, Bar, Bar Food

review: This French cafe at the bottom of the Peninsula hotel is a little busy and noisy, but it’s a good Streeterville option for a casual breakfast or lunch with tourists. Order the quiche Lorraine, then head straight to the Hancock Observatory.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Coffee & A Light Bite, Outdoor/Patio Situation, French, Bakery/Cafe

review: Katherine Anne's is a sweet shop that has an assortment of chocolates, candy, and marshmallows. But we come here primarily for one thing - their delicious hot chocolate. They have around 10 varieties (like salted caramel or vegan), and for $9 you can order a flight of three.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Bakery/Cafe

review: Bittersweet is a cafe in Lincoln Park with great baked goods. Come here for cake, cookies, or a cup of hot chocolate that's basically a melted chocolate bar.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Bakery/Cafe

review: Taste of Lebanon is one of the best places in Andersonville for a casual lunch. It’s a tiny spot with excellent chicken shawarma and fresh-baked pita. But no matter what you should get a bowl of the peppery lentil soup, which costs less than an ATM fee. Speaking of, they only accept cash so keep that in mind before you come.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Dining Solo, Lunch, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Middle Eastern

review: Little Victories is from the same people as Spilt Milk, and feels like a 70s rec room, with wood paneling and lots of plants. It’s a great bar for a first date because it’s got the necessities (dart boards, pool table, jukebox) but is nicer than the dive bar you were thinking about going to. Order the extra-battered french fries.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, First/Early in the Game Dates, Late Night Eats, Bar Food, Bar

review: This brewery taproom has plenty of seating and huge windows that make it feel bright and open all day. It’s dog-friendly and kid-friendly, so it’s perfect for spending a Saturday afternoon playing board games with your family and drinking some good beer.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Day Drinking, Dogs, Bar

review: This spot is from the same people as Victor Bar, and if you’ve ever been there you’ll know what to expect at Love Street: a dark cocktail bar with great drinks, helpful bartenders, and lots of people on dates. It’s perfect for pre-dinner drinks or grabbing a nightcap.
perfect_for_tags: Date Night, Drinking Good Cocktails, First/Early in the Game Dates, Bar

review: Carol’s is a divey honky-tonk in Uptown, and is a fun spot to stay out drinking and dancing to live country music until 4am. The food here is surprisingly great, with things like cheeseburgers, fried bologna sandwiches, and jumbo wings, and there are plenty of flat screens to watch the game if you’re not into country.
perfect_for_tags: Birthdays, Classic Establishment, Dancing, Eating At The Bar, Late Night Eats, Bar Food, Bar

review: This is a Chinese restaurant in Albany Park, but we come here primarily for one thing - the Korean wings. They're spicy, sticky and stay perfectly crispy under all the sauce. If you order correctly, you'll need a lot of water and napkins.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Chinese, Korean

review: Stocks and Blondes in the Loop both sounds and looks like the dirty basement bar you frequented in college. It’s like Rick’s in Ann Arbor, Kollege Klub in Madison, Kilroy’s in Bloomington, or whatever your version of that is. If you miss those days, stop in at Stocks and Blondes for an after-work drink.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Happy Hour, Bar

review: Miller’s has been open for over 80 years and feels like it’s from another era. It’s old school - with a huge bar, big booths, and a friendly staff encouraging you to have a drink at any hour of the day. Come here after work with a group, and make sure someone orders a martini.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Day Drinking, Bar Food, Bar

review: Great Central is a BYOF taproom that looks like a German beer hall, but one with ping pong tables and shuffleboard. This Near West Side spot (unsurprisingly) only brews German-style beer, but they have other breweries’ beer on tap too.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Day Drinking, Bar

review: Alulu is a small brewpub in Pilsen with excellent food. You’ll find tasty burgers and fish and chips along with Filipino-influenced dishes like tangy BBQ ribs with rice or crispy lumpia with a spiced dipping vinegar. The beer menu includes options like dry-hopped sours and Mexican lagers made with smoked poblano and jalapeno, and they come in flights with palate cleansers. Plus, the front wall is a retractable garage door, making it a great place to hang out on a nice day.
perfect_for_tags: Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Day Drinking, Drinks & A Light Bite, Lunch, Bar Food, Bar

review: This brew pub in Logan Square is all the way at the end of a residential street, and feels like a fun corner bar. Maplewood serves food like poutine and buffalo mac and cheese, and also distills their own booze, so the cocktail list doesn’t come across like an afterthought. Just know that it’s a small space, so on a busy night plan on standing for awhile.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Day Drinking, Eating At The Bar, Bar Food, Bar

review: On Tour is a taproom in West Town, and is the type of place where the people here are just as excited about Phish live streams as Bears games. It’s a nice, airy space (but not massive), and there’s a garage door that opens up when the weather’s warm. They have live music, and it’s an excellent place for day drinking.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Bar

review: We weren’t expecting a restaurant to be on the 18th floor of a building on the Northwestern hospital campus, but that’s exactly where we found Woodwind. The menu has strange-sounding-but-actually-delicious small plates like a sweet and savory Big Mac-inspired foie gras bao, and pomegranate roasted squash with chunky peanut butter, plus larger options like tender lamb ribs glazed with lavender and honey. The upscale space has a nice view of downtown, and the food makes it a fun option for dinner in Streeterville. Just try to ignore any “Code Blue” announcements while walking through the lobby.
perfect_for_tags: Business Meals, Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinking Good Wine, First/Early in the Game Dates, Impressing Out of Towners, American

review: Pilot Project in Logan Square has a bunch of small-batch breweries under one roof, which means there’s a wide variety of beers in their taproom. The space itself is comfortable, and opens much earlier than most brewery taprooms (7am on weekdays, 8am on weekends) to serve coffee and pastries.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Day Drinking, Drinks & A Light Bite, Bar

review: Fulton Galley is a food hall in Fulton Market with five rotating restaurants and a full bar, and it’s actually a comfortable place to have a meal. The tables won’t make you feel like you’re at a mall food court, and it has places like Italianette that have great food. The bar has TVs, free WiFi, and half off all drinks from 5-7pm on weekdays.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Dining Solo, Eating At The Bar, Happy Hour, Quick Eats, American, Latin

review: Budacki’s is a classic, cash-only hot dog stand in Ravenswood with a few picnic tables for outdoor seating. There’s a long menu of the usual suspects (like polishes, gyros, and pizza puffs), but the most exciting thing about this place is that you can get Crisp wings. Just be sure to hit an ATM on the way over.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Classic Establishment, Kids, Walk-Ins, American, Korean

review: Sweet Virginia’s is a small, counter-service breakfast spot in Ravenswood that’s useful to know about when you don’t feel like waiting for a table to open up at Over Easy. There are plenty of great takes on breakfast food like french toast and biscuits and gravy, but whatever you do, get an order of the homemade cinnamon sugar donuts.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Kids, American

review: The Long Room has an awesome craft beer list and serves coffee during the day, which makes it a good spot to get work done, catch up with friends, or go on a first date. In addition to the long bar that anchors the front room, there are a few big booths, a great patio out back, and a kitchen that serves food like biscuits and burgers until 1am.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Drinks & A Light Bite, Eating At The Bar, Late Night Eats, Bar
full_address: 1612 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60613

review: The first thing you need to know about Woodlawn Tap is that everyone calls it Jimmy’s - it’s one of those places that goes by an unofficial name, like the Sears Tower. Drinks are cheap and the food isn’t great, but good enough to get you through a long night of drinking here. Like most great dives, Jimmy’s is cash only.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, First/Early in the Game Dates, People Watching, Bar

review: Lincoln Park isn’t a neighborhood with a ton of character-heavy dives, which makes Rose’s extra special. There are couches that are almost certainly older than the ones in your parents’ basement, along with a pool table, a killer jukebox, free pretzels (or Bugles, depending on the night), and Christmas lights strung up year-round. Plan on ordering pitchers of beer or cocktails with two ingredients or less and you’ll have an excellent time. It’s cash only, so keep that in mind before you go.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, First/Early in the Game Dates, Bar

review: While Ipsento’s original location feels like your artsy friend’s messy apartment, their second shop just off the 606 trail has more of a sleek, wide-open feel to it. They’ve got pour overs, specialty lattes, nitro cold brew, some light bites, and a full bar starting at 11am. They’re only open until 9pm most nights, so it’s a good place for a post-dinner nightcap or a drink before an evening walk down the 606.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Date Night, Drinks & A Light Bite, First/Early in the Game Dates, Bakery/Cafe

review: Beck’s, the third spot from the team behind Toon’s and Pearl’s Southern Comfort, is a narrow Kansas City sports bar and grill in Lincoln Park with great double smash burgers. They have everything you need to keep a group happy during a football game, including TVs behind the bar, a solid draft list, airy front windows, baskets of tasty wings, and - in case your team is losing - some strong cocktails and an outdoor patio. In fact, all those things make it a great place for a casual meal in general, football optional. (But ordering the Beck’s Burger is mandatory.)
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Sports!, Bar Food

review: If you enjoy pairing your craft cocktails with a live DJ set or jazz combo, The Whistler is for you. But even if their eclectic slate of nightly live music isn’t your thing, the great drinks and undeniably cool atmosphere of this Logan Square bar/gallery/performance space are likely to convince you to show up on the early end, before any acts take the stage. The menu changes daily and most cocktails are $10 and under, so you should plan on hunkering down at the bar or on the cozy back patio until close, then returning to do the same thing the next day.
perfect_for_tags: Drinking Good Cocktails, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar

review: This Lakeview spot serves Italian-style thin-crust pizzas and craft cocktails, and it’s from the same owners as Dryhop Brewers next door. They manage to pull off the whole “industrial chic” thing in a way that doesn’t feel too cold, and you’ll feel welcomed and well-fed while you’re here. There are a number of interesting pizzas to choose from, but we recommend the Standard Bearer (soppressata, pickled jalapeno, and honey drizzle), which really lives up to its name. Sit at the bar for a fun glimpse into the pizza oven as you sip your drinks - there's a menu of spirit-free cocktails.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Eating At The Bar, Pizza, Italian

review: If you want some really good siu mai this weekend, but don’t want to wait for hours for a table, you’re in luck. Or, if your friend who’s somehow always free at 2pm during the week invites you to get some excellent pork buns, that’s possible too. That’s because D Cuisine, a small BYOB Chinese restaurant in Lincoln Park, serves these things all day. And while there are other dishes too, the condensed dim sum menu is really why you should come here - regardless of the time of day. D Cuisine doesn’t have a lot of tables, but it’s rarely crowded, so if you and your annoyingly carefree friend walk in, you shouldn’t have to wait. And since there are only about 30 dim sum dishes to choose from, it’s the type of place where you can be out in a half-hour (because you have to go back to work). Or you can spend that extra time discussing exactly how your apparently-unemployed friend can afford to live in a Lincoln Park brownstone. You’ll find a range of hits here, like steamed buns, siu mai, and perfectly chewy sesame balls. But the most impressive things are baked, like the BBQ pork buns, which have a sticky, sweet glaze. Or the egg yolk buns - soft and warm, with a gooey sweet filling that we’d put up against any cream-filled donut in town. There are a few things we don’t love - like the bland taro puffs or the dry Guangzhou roasted chicken - but larger entrees like the chow fun and string beans with pork floss are solid, and can help to round out your lunch or dinner. But our favorite reason for coming here is to eat reliably good buns and dumplings with a friend. And unlike your friend who mysteriously disappears for days at a time, then shows up with a black eye and a pocket full of cash - you can count on the dim sum here any time of day.
food_rundown:
Baked BBQ Pork Bun

The baked pork buns are one of our favorite things at D Cuisine. They’re the perfect mix of sweet and savory, coated in a sticky glaze, and taste like they just came out of the oven every time.


Steamed BBQ Pork Bun

These have the same great pork filling as the baked buns, but in a softer, doughier package. Definitely order these too.


Beef Chow Fun

The wide, pan-fried noodles are chewy and have crispy edges, and come with beef and vegetables. It’s good, but nothing you’ll be thinking about after you leave.


Siu Mai

The siu mai are perfectly steamed, and every springy bite has a nice balance of shrimp and pork.


String Beans With Pork Floss

This dish of slightly spicy, tender string beans with bits of crispy pork is a solid companion to the plethora of dumplings you’re about to eat. Make sure it’s on your table.


Deep-Fried Sesame Ball

These are chewy and delicious - we wish we had a few in our pocket to snack on throughout the day.


Guangzhou-Style Roasted Chicken

The roasted chicken is one of the daily specials from the full menu, and you can skip ordering it. The skin looks crispy but it’s actually just dry, and the meat is bland.


Deep-Fried Taro Puff

Another thing you can skip. These don’t have enough flavor to make up for how dry the filling is.


Baked Creamy Egg Yolk Bun

A warm muffin filled with molten egg custard, and something you definitely want to end your dim sum meal with - no matter what time of day it is.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, First/Early in the Game Dates, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Small Plates, Chinese, Dim Sum

review: Recess in the West Loop is a theme bar and restaurant that’s good at its gimmick, so it doesn’t feel forced or over-the-top. The theme is literally “Adult Playground” which means it’s a great place for just hanging out, or for lots of different activities, like bags or giant beer pong with trash cans. The drinks and food are fine (with bites like sliders and pigs in a blanket) and the space is huge, including an outdoor patio and plenty of tables.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Drinks & A Light Bite, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Sports!, American, Bar Food

review: The menu at Himalayan Sherpa Kitchen is long enough that you’re almost guaranteed to find something that fits your mood. Are you looking for something spicy or mild? Vegetarian or meaty? Deep-fried or curried? No matter what, there seems to be a traditional Nepali dish for that. The comfortable dining room is semiformal and quiet, so if you’re coming here with a loud talker, distract them with the delicious jhol momos (steamed dumplings in a tomato-based soup) and plenty of garlic naan.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Quiet Meals, Walk-Ins, Indian, Nepali

review: This quiet BYOB in Ravenswood has a long menu of Thai staples to choose from, and the highlights are the grilled pork neck salad and the combo platter of sausages (including isaan and sai ua). It’s pretty small, so try to think ahead and make a reservation - the dining area is almost always full. This is the type of place where you’ll want to know what all the surrounding tables ordered, and then order it for your own table to split.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Delivery, Lunch, Quiet Meals, Serious Take-Out Operation, Thai

review: Pick Me Up in Lakeview is the restaurant equivalent of your most broken-in pair of shoes: a comfortable, casual all-purpose neighborhood spot. It’s been around since 1997, and the whole menu is built around meatless and dairy-free options. There’s a ton of milkshakes, a long breakfast menu, and things like wraps, “pizzadillas,” and nachos. Beers and shots are also available, but they’re not the main focus here - you’ll usually find people doing work on laptops during the day, then hanging out afterward over diner food.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Late Night Eats, Lunch, Brunch, Vegetarian, Vegan

review: This large French restaurant in the Loop is open all day, and the main attraction here is a revolving bar that’s modeled after the famous Carousel Bar in New Orleans’ French Quarter. (You have to watch closely to see the carousel turning, because it’s very slow, only revolving once an hour.) The long menu is a little all over the place, but focuses mainly on French seafood dishes, with pastas, sandwiches, and salads in the mix too. Come here for a cocktail in the bar area and snack on a crab cake if you get hungry.
perfect_for_tags: Business Meals, Corporate Cards, American, French

review: River North is full of gigantic, sceney restaurants and expensive lunch options, so it makes sense if you haven’t noticed Fabcakes on Wells before - but that needs to change. This cafe serves housemade pastries, miniature quiches, and things like bagel sandwiches and paninis. The lattes come in unique flavors like vanilla rose and pepper fig, and the owner is always experimenting with new recipes, so you’ll find a new type of scone or tart available almost every day. It’s a low-key spot to get work done during the day, or to meet up with a friend for coffee.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Coffee & A Light Bite, Lunch, Quick Eats, Sandwiches, Bakery/Cafe

review: Just because you’re about to go see a fancy play in the theater district doesn’t mean you necessarily want an upscale meal. Or maybe you do. Roanoke has you covered either way, with cheap Happy Hour specials seven days a week (with choices like buffalo cauliflower and a pretty decent pizza of the day) and a three-course “pre-theater” prix fixe for $33. This is also a good spot to send exhausted holiday shoppers and a solid suggestion for after-work drinks if you work in the Loop.
perfect_for_tags: Happy Hour, Literally Everyone, Walk-Ins, American

review: You will not find credit card readers here. You will not find un-sticky menus. And you will not want it any other way. Golden House is a breakfast spot in the center of Uptown with more glittery vinyl seating and free coffee refills than you’ll know what to do with. The menu is standard diner food - you know exactly what these short stacks will taste like, and that’s what makes it a reliable spot. Head here before a show at the Riv or a day at the beach, choose between a booth or the counter seats, and eat your fill for under $10.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Cheap Eats, Classic Establishment, Diner

review: This spot on a quiet block in Roscoe Village is exactly where you want to unwind after work. There are weekday Happy Hour specials on their cocktails from 3-6pm (served out of cafeteria-style bubblers), and for $20 you can get everything on their limited menu: chips with three types of dip and a basket of four taquitos in various (and tasty) flavors. Sit inside or outside, play a game of Ms. Pac-Man, and watch reruns of old game shows above the bar. It’s like kicking back at home, except you get to say that you actually went out.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Drinks & A Light Bite, Bar Food, Bar

review: Simon’s is a Swedish-themed tavern in the heart of Andersonville, and it’s been open for over 85 years. It’s the rare spot that always seems to be crowded, but you’re never upset if you have to stand - in fact, you won’t be upset by anything at all once you try some of their Glogg (hot mulled wine) during the holidays, served with a spice cookie on the side. The Glogg is also available in the summertime as a slushie, along with their usual rotation of cheap beers on tap.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, Bar

review: Bandit is a smallish spot in the West Loop that feels like a party, but is still low-key enough for a casual get-together. The food is hit-or-miss, but the best things are small plates like the warm pretzel with Merkts cheese spread, the fried halloumi, and the charred carrots. Come here for drinks and bar snacks before a Big Night Out in the neighborhood.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American, Bar Food

review: Even though it’s surrounded by pricey boutiques and speakeasies that serve artisanal cocktails, The Flat Iron isn’t fancy. It’s just a 4am bar that plays loud music and has enough activities to keep you drinking here for hours, including pool, darts, skee-ball, shuffleboard, and Big Buck Hunter.
perfect_for_tags: People Watching, Bar

review: Fireside’s a worn-in bowling alley in Logan Square that’s been around since the 1940s. It’s not the cheapest place to bowl in town, but it’s got plenty of charm without leaning too hard on gimmicks or technology. There’s also a divey lounge with a pool table that's great for popping into before hitting the pricier bars in the neighborhood.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Classic Establishment, Sports!, Bar

review: Like a lot of places in Wrigleyville, Sluggers has sticky floors and enough rooms to make it feel more like an entertainment complex than a bar. But it’s also the only bar in Chicago we know of that has batting cages, so if that’s something you’ve been looking for, go here after a Cubs game and let ’er rip.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Sports!, Bar

review: Begyle’s taproom is one of our favorite stops on Malt Row, the two-mile stretch of breweries along the Ravenswood Corridor. It’s dog-friendly, rotating food trucks and pop-ups come through often, and they have skee-ball. During busier times, the upstairs is usually open with two more skee-ball machines as well as bags boards. Go on the weekends for yoga, bingo, and more fun things you don’t usually do at breweries.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Dogs, First/Early in the Game Dates, Bar

review: Big Joe’s is a great dive. The floors are carpeted, the beer is cheap, and on the nights when you’re the only person in the bar (which happens more often than you’d think), one of the friendly bartenders might unlock the pool table and give you free rein. But it’s the turtle races they host on Friday nights that make it spectacular. It’s packed to capacity, and because the more drinks you buy, the more chances you have to race, things get rowdy pretty quickly. Winners get free T-shirts, last place gets a free beer, and everyone else gets an excuse to buy more drinks.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, Day Drinking, Bar

review: This small cocktail bar in North Center serves craft cocktails and custom Old Fashioneds in a dim space with velvet curtains, exposed brick, and vintage light fixtures. This is a great spot for you and a date to start a night out. Just don’t arrive with a big group of friends, because you’d never all fit in here.
perfect_for_tags: Drinking Good Cocktails, Bar

review: Revolution’s brew pub in Logan Square is a popular spot for beer lovers, but their massive taproom in Avondale is just as worthy of a visit. They give tours of the production side of things, but if you’d rather just relax and drink there’s plenty of space for that too. They don’t serve food here, but it’s an excellent spot to BYOF, especially with Honey Butter Fried Chicken, which is a five-minute walk away.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Day Drinking, Bar

review: Archie’s is a pretty straightforward corner bar with a pool table, a great jukebox, and plenty of cheap beer. But the main thing that sets it apart from other Chicago dives is that it’s dog-friendly. There are lots of nights where there will be just as many Good Boys and Good Girls as barflies here, and that makes it an ideal place to drink in our book.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, Day Drinking, Dogs, Bar

review: One of Chicago’s funkier breweries, Off Color specializes in more experimental beers that you might not be able to find at some of the bigger taprooms in the city. Their space in Lincoln Park has the DIY charm of their label artwork, and it has an outdoor patio that’s great in the summer. We highly recommend you BYOF from Pizzeria Bebu just around the corner.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar

review: Situated at the very end of the Brown Line, right off the Kimball stop, Nighthawk has a distinct atmosphere: dive bar meets commuter cafe. It’s the type of coffee shop/bar hybrid we love, because unlike other all-day cafes scattered throughout the city, it feels like a bar here whether it’s 10am or 10pm. Big booths provide plenty of space to work, and there are enough outlets for everyone to keep their laptops charged. The coffee menu includes espresso drinks and cold brew, they’ve got a fairly long list of cocktails and craft beers available all day, and you can get a can of Hamm’s for $2.50.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, People Watching, Bar, Bakery/Cafe

review: You should go to Hing Kee in Chinatown for one reason: the handmade xiao long bao (soup dumplings). Sure, this casual spot has other stuff on the menu, but don’t worry about that. It’s the XLBs that need to be on the table. They’re made fresh daily, as evidenced by the person making them right in the front window. Get the pork, or pork with crab, and a scallion pancake while you’re at it.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Walk-Ins, Chinese

review: Joy Yee's has a food menu, but more importantly, it's one of the most popular boba spots in Chinatown - during the summer there’s always a crowd standing in front of the takeout window in Chinatown Square. Get the sweet rose with vanilla ice cream and strawberry jelly.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Chinese

review: Daguan Noodle in Chinatown has an interesting twist on hot pot: you pick out a type of noodle (we prefer the rice), a broth flavor (they’re all very good), and some sort of meat (meat’s always nice). You’ll receive your noodles, meat, and broth separately, with a bunch of tiny dishes of various veggies and mix-ins. Then it’s the servers who toss all the ingredients into the boiling broth in front of you. So it’s like hot pot, but without the crushing fear of overcooking everything.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Chinese, Hot Pot

review: Yummy Yummy in Chinatown got its start in the Richland Center food court, but now it’s a full-blown restaurant farther south on Wentworth, the only downside of which is that you might get distracted by the other equally great spots on the walk over. Order the beef tendon and fish ball soup, and be prepared for leftovers - the portions are huge (and very affordable).
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Chinese
full_address: 2334 S Wentworth Ave Ste 105, Chicago, IL 60616

review: There are two main decisions you need to make at Slurp Slurp in Chinatown: whether to order hand-pulled noodles or shaved, and whether you want them stir-fried or in a soup. Our favorite order here is a plate of the thick and chewy shaved noodles, fried with thinly sliced beef and vegetables. While you’re at it, get an order of steamed pork buns.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Chinese

review: MCCB is a sleek and bar-like Szechuan spot in Chinatown with a busy, upbeat atmosphere. The food here is salty and aggressively seasoned (we mean this in a good way), so BYOB plenty of drinks. They have really great twice-fried pork, cumin lamb, and dan dan noodles.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Serious Take-Out Operation, Chinese

review: There are so many restaurants in Chinatown, you will occasionally come across a good one that seems eerily deserted when you walk in. This might be the case at Dongpo, but don’t let that deter you - this place is great. Come here for dishes like spicy wontons, chili rabbit, and yu-shiang pork. The space is casual and BYOB.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Chinese

review: Xi’an Cuisine in Chinatown has some great noodle dishes, and that’s what you should focus on when you’re here. Particularly the lamb noodle soup with hand-stretched noodles and tender pieces of meat, or the biang biang noodles with pork, tomato, egg, and beef, both of which have a lot of flavor and just the right amount of spice.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Chinese

review: Ken Kee is a Chinatown utility player that works for a lot of occasions. It’s casual but still manages to feel special enough for date night, with a full bar and a long menu of consistently great food. Order standout dishes like the fried noodles, tender short ribs in a savory XO sauce, or fish in black bean sauce, then finish up with an order of man tao (fried bread with condensed milk).
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, First/Early in the Game Dates, Chinese

review: Sze Chuan Cuisine in Chinatown serves reliable Szechuan food in an upscale, trendy environment. Everything here is tingly and spicy the way you expect it to be, and their chongqing chicken and mala fish fillet are particularly great. But if you’re not into those options, this place also has some solid hot pot, and you can get a combo of up to three broths.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, First/Early in the Game Dates, Chinese, Hot Pot

review: Triple Crown’s food can be pretty average, but when you want dim sum in a classic space in the old part of Chinatown, it does the trick. The quality can really vary depending on the time of day you’re here. Come earlier on the weekend when the restaurant is at its busiest, because the dim sum will be made more frequently and tends to be fresher.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Classic Establishment, Lunch, Walk-Ins, Chinese, Dim Sum

review: Daebak is a solid Korean barbecue spot in Chinatown. This place is only a few years old, and feels like it - it has an industrial atmosphere and K-pop music videos projected all over the walls. The attentive servers are very good about turning your meat over the gas grill and refilling your banchan - and refills are very important, because everything is fantastic. Don’t leave without ordering a kimchi pancake.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Drinking Good Cocktails, Korean, BBQ

review: Bonchon is a Korean fried chicken chain that’s worth knowing about if you’re in Chinatown. It’s right in the center of Chinatown Square, and while the sauces don’t quite measure up to the ones at Crisp or Dak, the food here is consistently tasty. Get a half-and-half order of the spicy and garlic wings and some beer.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Walk-Ins, Korean

review: If you’ve walked through Chinatown Square, you’ve definitely noticed the ducks hanging in the window at BBQ King House. As that might indicate, this place indeed specializes in duck, though all the juicy roasted meats here are fantastic. While the duck is a must order, you can’t go wrong with pork or chicken, either - just get here early, because they tend to run out of the most popular stuff at night.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Quick Eats, Walk-Ins, Chinese

review: When it’s 3am and you want sizzling beef, salt and pepper squid, congee, or just about anything else, Chi Cafe in Chinatown is your answer. This place is open 8am-4am almost every day of the week and stays open 24 hours on weekends, which means it has you covered for breakfast, second breakfast, lunch, dinner, second dinner, drunk dinner, and hangover. The menu is long, so make sure your friend you’ve been out with all night doesn’t fall asleep while deciding what to order. Be prepared for this place to get slammed when the bars close.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Breakfast, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Late Night Eats, Lunch, Walk-Ins, Chinese

review: Situated on a side street off Wentworth in Chinatown, Go 4 Food seems small, but there’s an upstairs that can be used for private parties. They’re known for their fresh seafood - there’s a tank filled with lobster and crab right in the back of the dining room - and there are always some specials that shouldn’t be overlooked. Our favorite appetizer is the bao “taco,” and as far as entrees, the slightly sweet walnut shrimp and the chili spiced dungeness crab are standouts (though all the seafood entrees are great).
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Chinese

review: If you want sushi near McCormick Place, then South Coast is a solid option. The space is sleek and upscale, and while there are a few other locations (Evanston and a BYOB spot in Wicker Park), this is one with a full bar. Order some small plates like gyoza and edamame in addition to some rolls - the spicy tuna and the white dragon maki with sweet potato tempura are both good.
perfect_for_tags: Business Meals, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Corporate Cards, Drinking Good Cocktails, Impressing Out of Towners, Quiet Meals, Sushi

review: Kroll's is a sports bar near McCormick Place in the South Loop. This spot has a long menu of typical bar food, including a selection of perfectly fine burgers. Come here if you’re in the neighborhood for a conference and want to grab a beer and a quick meal.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Sports!, American, Bar Food

review: If you would like to visit a neighborhood coffee shop that doesn’t have its own app or an entire pumpkin spice agenda, go to The Spoke & Bird. This spot near McCormick Place has a nice outdoor patio and a short food menu that includes sandwiches and salads, plus they serve beer, wine, and cocktails.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Lunch, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Walk-Ins, American, Bakery/Cafe

review: Would we suggest that someone from Vancouver or Maine come here? Probably not. But if you’re near McCormick Place and need a dinner spot, consider Chicago Oyster House a valid option. They have a variety of decent oysters, along with things like crab legs, sushi, and steak in an upscale space. Get the fresh oysters, anything fried, and skip the sushi.
perfect_for_tags: Business Meals, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Corporate Cards, Seafood

review: 14 Parish is an upscale Carribean restaurant, and it’s one worth seeking out if you’re in the South Loop. You’ll find dishes like jerk chicken and catfish, oxtails, and vegetarian curry. The food here is really good (especially if you’re a fan of spice) and the service is really friendly. Just be aware that they do a lot of private events here, so the atmosphere can feel scattered if you come during a graduation, birthday party, or on the weekend during wedding season.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Small Plates, Vegetarians, Caribbean

review: There are a few locations of this reliably good Thai spot in Chicago. This one happens to be near McCormick Place and is ideal if you’re looking for a nice quiet meal in the neighborhood. The atmosphere is relaxed and the service is friendly. Order pad thai or pad see ew, and plan on having leftovers.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Quiet Meals, Serious Take-Out Operation, Thai

review: La Cantina Grill is a sit-down Mexican spot in the South Loop near McCormick Place. The menu has things like nachos, enchiladas, burritos, and fajitas. Come here for an upbeat group dinner that involves plenty of margaritas.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Business Meals, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Corporate Cards, Latin, Mexican

review: There are a number of Harold’s in the city, and these casual counter spots all focus on fried chicken and fish, plus things like fries, coleslaw, and spicy wings. Not all locations are created equal (they can vary in service and quality), but the one near McCormick Place is reliably good.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, American, Southern

review: Pizano’s is a local chain that’s been around since 1991, and this is the location right across the street from McCormick Place. This spot has both thin crust and deep dish, though we’re going to suggest you go with the thin. We appreciate the buttery cracker crust, and we always order it with pepperoni. If it’s nice out, sit on the patio.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Delivery, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Serious Take-Out Operation, Strollers, Pizza, Pasta

review: Il Culaccino is an Italian restaurant that’s right across the street from McCormick Place. The large, somewhat generic space feels a lot like a chain restaurant, but the huge portions of pasta and tasty appetizers are better than what you’d find at one of those places. Order the spicy shrimp arrabbiata or the gnocchi al forno - it’s cheesy, tasty, and exactly what you want from a red-sauce pasta.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Impressing Out of Towners, Italian

review: Delilah’s is a versatile bar in a neighborhood where most bars only do one thing well, or more often, nothing much at all. It’s a place with over 800 whiskeys and 200 beers, where there’s local art on the walls and all types of music being DJed nightly. Not only is it better than most bars in Lincoln Park, it’s better than most bars in the city.
perfect_for_tags: First/Early in the Game Dates, Bar

review: Rainbo Club is a gritty dive on the edge of a neighborhood that hardly has any gritty dives anymore. Cheap drinks, big booths, a long bar, and a legendary photobooth have made this an awesome spot to hang out at for decades.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, People Watching, Bar

review: Sportsman’s Club is a bar in Ukrainian Village that combines its divey history with new and exciting drinks. Whether you’re hanging inside or on the low-key back patio, you can expect to have a good time.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, First/Early in the Game Dates, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar

review: The Matchbox is the smallest bar in the city, and it makes some of the better classic cocktails around. If you roll your eyes when people talk about making friends at bars, come here - you’re in such close quarters that it’s impossible for conversations not to overlap and intersect until you've got a new group of drinking buddies.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, People Watching, Bar

review: A classic, dingy dive that's one of the only places in the city where you can buy a pack of cigarettes and smoke them right in the bar. Make sure you have money for the jukebox, and if you do, then make sure you have quarters for your laundry the next day.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, People Watching, Bar

review: Slashies - liquor stores slash bars - are big in Chicago, which is great for when you want to keep the party rolling after you leave. But we wouldn’t blame you if you never wanted to leave Maria’s. Well-decorated and well-stocked, it’s also attached to Kimski, an excellent Polish-Korean counter-service spot. It’s the type of bar you want to close down every time you go.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Eating At The Bar, First/Early in the Game Dates, Late Night Eats, Bar Food, Bar

review: Big Chicks is a casual, slightly divey LGBTQ bar on Sheridan in Uptown. The crowd can get wild, but it’s generally more low-key than some of the more sceney bars in Boystown. They have popular food specials like a $1 burger on Monday nights, and since it’s attached to Tweet, the bar food here is better than most.
perfect_for_tags: Dancing, Day Drinking, Eating At The Bar, Late Night Eats, Bar Food, Bar

review: Sidetrack is an event. It’s the standout spot in Northalsted, a neighborhood full of great LGBTQ bars, and that’s partly because it keeps the party going all week long with a lineup of show tune sing-alongs and drag shows. It’s usually packed here, but even on its clubbiest nights there’s more than enough space to find a change of scenery if you need to.
perfect_for_tags: Birthdays, Dancing, Day Drinking, See And Be Seen, Bar

review: Whirlaway is a true neighborhood bar in Logan, anchored by the owner and bartender, Maria. Come to drink cheap beer here and you’ll become a regular soon enough, chatting with her and the other regulars about life.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, People Watching, Bar

review: The Hideout is in a small old house in the middle of an industrial yard - and it’s one of the best cultural hubs in the city. Music, comedy, podcasts, political panels, and more are hosted here, a place where you can get a cheap drink any night of the week. They also have a great dance party every Saturday at midnight.
perfect_for_tags: Live Music, Dancing, Outdoor/Patio Situation, People Watching, Bar

review: Guthrie’s is probably best known for its wall of board games, and that definitely helps make it one of the best first date spots in the city. But the cozy atmosphere, solid selection of craft beer, and screened-in back porch also help. It’s an oasis of calm that’s rare this close to Wrigley Field, and a great place to hang out for hours at a time.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, Day Drinking, First/Early in the Game Dates, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar

review: The Cove Lounge is a dive near the University of Chicago in Hyde Park with a semi-nautical theme and a ton of character. The big wooden tables are perfect for gathering a group to talk politics over a beer or seven, while the giant mural of President Obama watches over you.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, People Watching, Bar

review: Kingston Mines is one of the best spots in the city to see live music, with blues shows going until late at night seven days a week. Plus, there’s a full food menu to tide you over while you watch.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, Dancing, Eating At The Bar, Late Night Eats, BBQ, Bar

review: Maybe the most historic place to drink in the city, The Green Mill in Uptown was one of Al Capone’s favorite haunts back in the day. Although you can’t see the secret underground tunnels he and his pals used to sneak in and out of the club, you should come for the late-night jazz on the weekends, along with some of the stiffest gin martinis in town.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, First/Early in the Game Dates, Impressing Out of Towners, Bar

review: Cole’s is a hip-but-not-too-hip Logan Square hangout with fairly cheap drinks and a decent crowd most nights. There are free comedy and rock shows in the back room, so be sure to catch the next big thing here before they blow up.
perfect_for_tags: First/Early in the Game Dates, Bar

review: The Chicago Diner is an institution that’s been around since the early ’80s and still draws a crowd on the weekends. There’s another location in Logan Square, but the one on Broadway is the original. Everything on the menu is either vegan or can be made vegan, with seitan, tempeh, and tofu showing up in a lot of the dishes. There are diner classics like pancakes, biscuits and gravy, and omelets, but they’ve also got a meatless take on things like gyros, wings, and poutine. Just be sure to get a milkshake while you’re here - they’re delicious.
perfect_for_tags: Brunch, Kids, Vegans, Vegetarians, Diner, Vegetarian

review: This modern Greek restaurant in Lincoln Park is one of a few locations of Avli, and it’s on a quiet side street that makes their sidewalk seating a nice outdoor option in the neighborhood. They have a list of Greek wines and specialty cocktails with Greek spirits, and grabbing drinks is the best move here, since the food is pretty bland. Get the spicy feta if you need a light bite.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Greek

review: Wood is your typical New American restaurant. The wide-ranging menu appeals to pretty much everyone, with small and large plates, flatbreads, pastas, and a cheeseburger. The food here isn’t going to shock and/or amaze you, but it tastes great, and almost everything is made in house. Come here for drinks and a casual meal.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, American

review: The Gundis is a low-key spot on Clark that’s perfect for an easy dinner with friends. But it’s also great in the morning - the full Kurdish breakfast is a spread for two that includes three cheeses, three house jams, honey, butter, sesame butter, vegetables, fries, fried cheese rolls, and your choice of egg scramble. The Kurdish baklawa crepes are another great breakfast dish that pairs well with their Kurdish coffee, which is made from pistachio beans. If you’re someone who reliably orders two eggs and toast wherever you go, this is an excellent place to branch out.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Kurdish

review: If you’re ever trying to get into Tango Sur and the wait is two hours, consider calling an audible and heading to Bodega Sur next door. It’s not BYOB, so you’re going to have to ditch the wine bottle you brought with you. But since they have a full bar, that just means you can drink a mojito with the same delicious Argentine steak that made Tango Sur a neighborhood destination. They’re open for lunch and brunch every day, plus they have a retail section with plenty of South American wine bottles to go.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, First/Early in the Game Dates, Lunch, Steaks, Argentinian

review: You’re bound to see a lot of families at Frasca, and it’s earned its reputation as a neighborhood staple. The wood-fired pizzas are reliably delicious, and there are enough Italian favorites rounding out the menu to make everyone happy. Try the Italian sausage pizza with crumbled fennel sausage and sauteed onions, or the rigatoni gigante served in a great tomato cream sauce. Bottles of wine are half off on Mondays, which should instantly make you feel better about riding the brown line here from work at rush hour.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Happy Hour, Kids, Pizza, Pasta

review: Considering that most of the options near the intersection of Belmont and Sheffield are fast-casual spots or late-night eats, Figo is a nice addition to the neighborhood. It’s a wine bar serving reasonably priced small plates, with pastas that are all under $15. The comfortable atmosphere is enough to make this a good spot for a weeknight date or a stop before a night out at the Vic. If you don’t have tickets to a show, you can just split a bottle of wine and watch as drunk people file into Trader Todd’s for karaoke across the street.
