perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Drinking Good Wine, Eating At The Bar, Wine Bar, Italian

review: The best thing about The Dawson in River West is the giant patio. As far as the food goes, the food is fine (you’ll find dishes like mussels, mac and cheese, and a cheeseburger) but we come here mainly for drinks, and to sit outside under some string lights.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Drinking Good Cocktails, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American

review: Carnivale is a Latin restaurant in Fulton Market with a wide range of influences. You’ll find dishes like ropa vieja, empanadas, and paella. The colorful space is huge and great for groups, so expect to be surrounded by diners celebrating birthdays, retirements, and eighth-grade graduations. (Though probably not at the same table).
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Drinking Good Cocktails, Private Dining, Latin

review: Wildberry now has a few locations in Chicago and the surrounding suburbs, but this one on Randolph is conveniently located for tourists, just across from Millennium Park and near several hotels. The menu is as long as you'd expect from a chain breakfast place, featuring crepes, Belgian waffles, and some French toasts that are basically desserts (red velvet cake, churro, and s'mores options, among others). Come here when you need a post-shopping-trip consensus option.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Lunch, American

review: There are lots of Chicago locations of the Original Pancake House, but this one somehow feels the most original. It’s a tiny restaurant that sits between much larger and more impressive buildings, like a little time capsule. It’s cramped inside, so expect a long wait on weekends, but know that the wait will be worth it: they deliver the goods when it comes to pancakes, and they have a great Dutch Baby on special.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Diner

review: Eleven City Diner is a deli near the Museum Campus in the South Loop. Come here for things like pastrami and corned beef sandwiches or all-day breakfast dishes like their black and white french toast made with challah.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Breakfast, Brunch, Dining Solo, Lunch, Deli

review: Do you like kids and strollers? Then you’ll enjoy eating at Bakin’ & Eggs, a family-friendly weekday breakfast spot in Lakeview.  The menu has the usual suspects (pancakes, French toast, and biscuits and gravy) along with a number of frittatas. And in case screaming children might stress you out (yours or someone else’s), it might interest you to know that they also serve cocktails.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Kids, Strollers, American

review: Southport & Irving is a neighborhood bar and restaurant in Lakeview. It’s a convenient spot in the neighborhood for grabbing drinks and American food like sandwiches, salads, or grilled salmon. Also worth knowing about: on the weekend they have bottomless brunch.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Drinking Good Cocktails, Eating At The Bar, American

review: Angelina’s is an Italian restaurant that’s been in Lakeview for over 30 years. And while there are much better spots for Italian food in the city, this place has a fun weekend brunch. The menu is short and uncomplicated (with dishes like French toast and a frittata), with a bottomless mimosa package.
perfect_for_tags: Brunch, Day Drinking, Italian

review: Zia’s is an Italian restaurant in Lakeview that’s primarily useful for two reasons: it has a large patio that’s great for groups, and a bottomless brunch special on the weekend. The food is average, but it's a fun neighborhood option as long as you know what you’re getting into. During the summer this place gets very crowded, and if you’re here for brunch, there’s a two-hour time limit.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Brunch, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Italian

review: It’s entirely possible to eat at this fantastic Scandinavian breakfast spot in North Park and pretend you’re actually at a French cafe in Sweden. If time allows, sit for a Belgian waffle or Oslo omelette with smoked salmon - but know that it’s also worth grabbing a danish or cinnamon roll on the go.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Scandinavian

review: RL is right off the Magnificent Mile, which means it’s full of tourists who like shopping at upscale clothing stores and eating at restaurants located inside upscale clothing stores. RL sits in the Ralph Lauren building, serving perfectly fine yacht-club-style food like mini lobster rolls, calamari, and crab cakes.
perfect_for_tags: Brunch, Business Meals, Corporate Cards, Dinner with the Parents, People Watching, American

review: Batter & Berries is a weekday breakfast spot in Lincoln Park that’s known for its French toast. It’s their specialty, and they have options like blueberry, strawberry, lemon, and caramel. But the best strategy is to order the flight, which has all four. If sweet breakfasts aren’t your thing, order one of their deconstructed omelettes.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, American

review: Pannenkoeken are large, thin pancakes traditionally found in the Netherlands and Belgium, and Pannenkoeken Café is a cute breakfast spot in Lincoln Square that specializes in making them. It’s a very small restaurant with limited seating, but even on weekends you won’t have much of a wait. They have egg dishes and French toast, but you should stick with the pannenkoeken - either sweet variations like chocolate banana, or savory options like bacon and cheese (the bacon is actually in the batter).
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Belgian

review: Dolo is one of our favorite spots in Chinatown for dim sum. And it stands out from other spots in the neighborhood by having a full bar, and because it has a shorter menu. But don’t let that discourage you - you’ll find a lot of the usual suspects, including pork buns, shumai, and sesame balls. Everything is made to order (there are no carts being rolled around) and tastes delicious.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Brunch, Drinking Good Cocktails, Chinese, Dim Sum

review: As tends to happen with the busiest breakfast spots in the city, Kanela has multiplied. There are six locations now, but this is the original, still serving their popular Greek-influenced brunch. There are at least four options for French toast on a given day, and plenty of different egg dishes. Be sure to get some of the sweet cinnamon monkey bread to split for the table.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, American, Greek

review: The Front Room is a dimly lit restaurant and cocktail bar in the West Loop that serves tasty New Orleans-inspired food. You'll find things like a cheese plate, lobster campanelle, and grilled salmon. Also valid is just coming here for cocktails and a seat on their patio.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Drinking Good Cocktails, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, French, Southern

review: Giordano’s is a deep dish pizza chain. While it’s not our favorite (that would be Lou Malnati’s, it’s still very satisfying. And this is a perfectly valid choice if you decide to stay at Navy Pier. The pizza here is stuffed deep dish, which means it’s double crusted, with tomato sauce on top and about 25 pounds of cheese inside.
perfect_for_tags: Pizza

review: Even though it looks like an old community center from the outside, Sleeping Village in Avondale is actually a hip bar and music venue with a nice fenced-in patio. There are over 30 draft options, making it an ideal place to get a beer before or after a show. In addition to larger concerts, they host free events with food pop-ups and local bands or DJs.
perfect_for_tags: Dancing, Day Drinking, First/Early in the Game Dates, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar

review: This taproom in Bowmanville is the newer, larger location of North side favorite Half Acre Beer Company, serving all of your favorites on draft as well as brewery exclusives. As for food, they have solid Roman-style pizza and mains like a half chicken and spicy pork sandwich, along with a full Sunday brunch menu. There’s also a patio complete with an outside bar and a bocce court.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Dogs, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American, Bar Food

review: Estereo is an all-day, dog-friendly party in Logan Square. In the summer, when the garage door walls are open and the vintage Latin vinyl is spinning, there’s no better place to drink. There are cocktails based around Latin American spirits like pisco, raicilla, and cachaça, and the Breezy (their house cocktail) is a carbonated mixture of yerba mate, falernum, lime, and your spirit of choice.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Drinking Good Cocktails, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar

review: A bright, minimalist brewery in Logan Square, Hopewell sort of feels like the lobby of a start-up, but one where everyone’s having fun and enjoying their lives. Decorated with light wood and white walls, the space is usually bustling - you’ll find groups of people working on laptops, playing board games, or just talking, and both dogs and outside food are welcome. If you’re not drinking one of their drafts, their eight-ounce Lil’ Buddy is the cutest can of beer you’ll find in Chicago.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Dogs, First/Early in the Game Dates, Bar

review: The biggest issue with this spot in Chinatown is deciding to shorten the name to “Chef Xiong” or “Taste of Szechuan” when we’re telling people to come here. Whatever you decide to call it, the important thing is that this upscale BYOB spot has really good food. The menu is long enough to have been written by George RR Martin, but we’re big fans of the cold jelly noodles in a perfectly spicy black bean sauce, the grilled pork ribs, and the wontons in chili sauce.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Kids, Chinese

review: With a chalkboard menu, green lunch trays, and plastic tablecloths, Feed feels like a down-home Southern cafeteria - with cafeteria prices. For under $10, you can get a juicy, well-seasoned quarter rotisserie chicken and pick two sides from a list that we can’t count on two hands. As a bonus, it’s BYOB, and there’s a hidden little patio perfect for family dinners in the summertime.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Walk-Ins, Southern

review: Café Colao has something we wish all coffee shops served: Puerto Rican pastries. In addition to their coffee and bakery menu they’ve also got a long list of breakfast and lunch sandwiches, from steak and eggs to medianoches. There’s no wifi, but there is sidewalk seating perfect for that coffee date you’ve been putting off, or you can take your iced latte for a walk around the park a block away.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Coffee & A Light Bite, Bakery/Cafe

review: Dante’s is a solid place to grab a New York-style slice and pair it with an excellent draft beer. They rotate slices of their specialty pizzas daily, along with a vegan option. They also have a back patio with plastic seats if you want to eat your pizza in the open air instead of a dark bar.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Eating At The Bar, Vegans, Walk-Ins, Pizza

review: Diana’s is an affordable diner with awesome Puerto Rican sandwiches. They offer a half-dozen ways to eat plantains, including alcapurrias, maduras, tostones, and mofongo. This place closes in the early evening, so it’s best to come in for breakfast or lunch. Or breakfast and lunch so you can work your way through all those different plantain dishes.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Dining Solo, Lunch, Walk-Ins, Caribbean

review: Humboldt Haus has some of the most satisfying deli sandwiches in the city, made on fresh bread with hearty portions of meat and cheese and finished with extras like creamy garlic mayo and Haus dressing. Because it’s attached to a liquor store it has a full bar, but being across the street from Humboldt Park, it’s also perfect for picnic supplies if you don’t dine in.
perfect_for_tags: Dining Solo, Eating At The Bar, Lunch, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, American, Sandwiches

review: Rootstock is a low-key restaurant that serves dinner until 1am and always has a long list of wine and bottled beer available to order. Along with their seasonal menu, they make a solid burger, and if you’re not coming for a full meal, you can split one of their rotating charcuterie and cheese boards.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Drinking Good Wine, Late Night Eats, Wine Bar

review: Papa’s is a casual Puerto Rican restaurant in Humboldt Park that serves excellent jibaritos. The dining room is small, but there’s a covered patio out front where you and a friend can split a BYOB six-pack.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Walk-Ins, Caribbean

review: Lola’s is a hot dog stand that serves Detroit-style coney dogs - pork-and-beef sausages covered in chili. The dogs here have a great snap, and the chili is a fun change of pace from the typical Chicago fixings (although they offer those, too). To drink, there’s Faygo, Vernors, and a few milkshake options, the most exciting of which is the Sanders Bumpy Cake Shake, made with a Detroit delicacy involving devil’s food cake, buttercream frosting, and fudge icing.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Kids, Lunch, Quick Eats, Hot Dogs

review: Taco El Jalisciense is a small counter-service Mexican restaurant serving quick and delicious food. The tacos here are solid, with plenty of choices, but the reason you’ll want to stop in is the fresh guacamole, which comes in two sizes. Get the large.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Dining Solo, Quick Eats, Mexican, Tacos

review: Casual spots where you can easily stop in for pasta and a glass of wine are useful to know about, and if you’re in River North, Torchio is a solid option for both of these things. The pastas are made in house, and you’ll find dishes like cacio e pepe, spaghetti carbonara, and tagliatelle with a pretty tasty bolognese served in a parmesan basket that, unfortunately, sounds better than it is. None of them are worth going out of your way for, but just fine if you’re in the neighborhood. The space is small and gets pretty loud, so don’t come here expecting to work on your novel.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Drinking Good Wine, Pasta, Wine Bar

review: This is an upscale diner in the Tri-Taylor neighborhood. You’ll find classics like skillets, waffles, and omelettes ranging from really great (like the skillet with eggs, fried chicken, and gravy) to average (the greasy Monte Cristo). While you shouldn’t drive across town for the food here, it’s good for a hangover breakfast or brunch in the neighborhood.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Brunch, Diner

review: Kie-Gol-Lanee is a BYOB Mexican restaurant in Uptown specializing in Oaxacan food. The menu has tamales wrapped in a plantain leaf with your choice of fillings (our favorite is the pork), tlayudas (crispy tortillas topped with beans, cheese, cabbage, tomatoes, onions, and meat), and entrees like a flavorful rabbit stew in a yellow mole. The servers are friendly, and the relaxed space is great for groups. Come here with friends and a few bottles of wine and see who starts talking about their ex first.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Mexican

review: Despite what the entire world thinks, Chicago isn’t just a deep dish city, and we’ll happily make room for a place like Robert’s. The highlight here is the flavorful, airy, slightly crispy thin crust. You’ll find a variety of toppings, from fennel with pepperoni and honey, to sausage with caramelized onions. While the crust is always excellent, the topping combinations aren’t always balanced. That said, it’s worth a visit if you’re anywhere near Navy Pier and want pizza options besides Giordano’s.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Pizza

review: El Chubasco is a small, charming restaurant in Pilsen that’s always full of families and people stopping in for takeout. The menu is long, but we like focusing on tacos while we’re here. The handmade tortillas here are small and light, and doubled up to withstand the filling. Our favorite taco is the Cecina (guacamole, beans, pico de gallo), but the carne asada is very good too.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Mexican, Tacos

review: It can be uncomfortable when you walk into a party and immediately get the feeling that the hosts have been arguing about something - who was supposed to pick up brie for the cheese tray, maybe, or the best way to calm their dachshund around guests. Hopefully, making a beeline for the drinks and some Trader Joe’s mushroom turnovers will distract you from the tension you’re sensing. The atmosphere at Cebu, a Filipino restaurant in Wicker Park, can feel a little like that tense party. But if you focus on the tasty food and whoever you’re with, you’ll have a good time. Thankfully, the great dishes on Cebu’s menu make it possible to ignore what you’re pretty sure are the sounds of the staff arguing with each other. An intensely flavorful chicken adobo and perfectly tender pork BBQ skewers are both great ways to keep yourself occupied. The beef tapa is also very good, with slightly caramelized meat marinated in a delicious calamansi and soy sauce, and ordering the soft and sweet housemade pandesal buns is non-negotiable - they’re delicious and they have to be on the table. As you eat, you can watch the halo-halo being carefully assembled at the dessert station, which is also a soothing diversion. When food falls short here, it’s when it’s inconsistent. The lumpia is occasionally burnt and greasy. Sometimes the egg on the sisiq is undercooked, sometimes it’s overcooked. The specials are a mixed bag of hits like the moist pork belly lechon with crispy skin and misses like a very dry adobo burger that comes with some unbearably salty fries. But everything is affordable enough that it’s not the end of the world if you play lumpia roulette and lose. Even if you are winning at roulette, you probably still won’t be able to avoid hearing what’s going on behind the scenes here. The restaurant’s small, narrow space and semi-open kitchen mean that everything - whether it’s snarky back-and-forths or fallout from a messed-up drink order - is noticeable. It’s a lot like your party hosts whisper-fighting in the hallway of their tiny apartment: at best it’s a little awkward, at worst it’s downright unpleasant. Cebu does have a very nice, secluded back patio, though, and if you sit out there, you and your dinner date can focus on your own petty arguments. Even if their stressed-out party hosts can’t get it together, that doesn’t mean the guests can’t still have fun. If there are drinks, good food, and other partygoers to keep you occupied, you can leave the couple to discuss the dachshund’s anxiety levels among themselves. The same applies at Cebu. Get some chicken adobo and just try to let the tension roll off your back. After all, it gives you something to talk about on the way home.
food_rundown:
Pandesal

The rolls are perfectly soft and slightly sweet, served with a honey butter you’ll want to ask for about four extra servings of. You need these.


Chicken Adobo

The chicken adobo is another must order. The bone-in chicken thigh is tender, and the vinegary adobo sauce is perfectly balanced with some coconut milk. Order it with a side of garlic rice and save some pandesal to soak up whatever’s left of the sauce.


BBQ Pork

The perfectly tender pork shoulder is served on skewers and marinated in a mixture of pineapple, ketchup, soy sauce, and garlic. It’s sweet, savory, and absolutely delicious.


Flap Steak

We really like this. The steak slices are marinated in soy sauce and citrusy calamansi, and have slightly caramelized edges. It comes with a side of rice that tastes great after soaking up the extra marinade.


Bam-I

This noodle dish is a combination of both egg and glass noodles, chicken, pork belly, Chinese sausage, and tossed with banana ketchup, oyster sauce, and soy sauce. Considering how much is going on here it’s surprisingly light, and a little bland. But the flavor that _is_ there is great. Order this for the table to share.


Sisiq

The sisiq is delicious but inconsistent. It’s made with pork mask, duck liver, jalapeno, and a fried egg. Every time we’ve had it it’s been a little different. Sometimes the yolk is completely cooked. Sometimes the white is runny. Sometimes there are a lot of peppers, sometimes not. It’s a gamble, but if you like pork cheek and liver, it’s worth ordering.


Kinilaw


Kinilaw is a nice, light ceviche, and the one at Cebu is very bright and flavorful. The tuna is dressed in a calamansi and coconut broth that complements it perfectly.


Lumpia

The lumpia (Filipino eggrolls) at Cebu are a crapshoot. We’ve had it cooked perfectly where it’s crispy and golden brown, and we’ve had it when it’s extremely greasy and burnt to hell. Order at your own risk.


Adobo Burger

The burger pops on and off the menu - occasionally it’s on the regular one, and occasionally it’s on the list of specials. The patty is glazed with adobo and comes with bacon, havarti, and sriracha garlic aioli. The most intriguing thing about it is that it comes on a housemade pandesal bun, but that can’t save the meat, which is really dry.


Lechon Belly

If you like pork belly, you’ll love this. The roasted belly is stuffed with onion, garlic, lemongrass, and anise, and the skin is very crispy. They make a limited amount and frequently run out.


Halo-Halo


Cebu’s desserts are great, and you shouldn’t leave without getting one. A standout is the halo-halo, which has enough stuff (shaved ice, evaporated milk, cherries, red bean paste, jelly, cornflakes, maybe Jimmy Hoffa, a housemade cookie) to keep you entertained for a long time.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Dining Solo, Drinking Good Cocktails, Filipino

review: Larry’s is a small bar  with great cocktails from the people behind Heritage Bikes & Coffee in the lobby of the Lawrence House. Come do some people-watching here before a show at the Aragon, or relax on the back patio during the summer.
perfect_for_tags: Drinking Good Cocktails, People Watching, Bar

review: GMan is a neighborhood bar in Wrigleyville with a solid beer list, as well as live music and other events. Its low-key atmosphere makes it a welcome change from the Cubs bars and shiny new restaurant complexes that make up most of the area.
perfect_for_tags: Bar

review: La Sala is a mezcal bar in the basement of La Luna, a Mexican restaurant in Pilsen. They have good cocktails, a loungy atmosphere, and a shuffleboard table. It’s a great place to grab a drink before or after a show at Thalia Hall down the street.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Bar

review: Ludlow Liquors in Avondale is a polished version of a neighborhood dive. It has a colorful back patio and a kitchen named Old Habits that serves unconventional takes on bar food classics. They also serve some cocktails in single or double pours, so you can try more and spend less.
perfect_for_tags: Drinking Good Cocktails, Eating At The Bar, First/Early in the Game Dates, Late Night Eats, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar Food, Bar

review: Lazy Bird is in the basement of The Hoxton hotel in the West Loop, and it’s the type of intimate mid-century lounge that might never have actually existed outside of a movie set. A beautiful marble bar serving updates on 52 classic cocktails anchors the room, but there are plenty of dark shadows to slink back into if you’re trying to stay incognito for whatever reason. Come here while you’re waiting for a table at Cabra upstairs.
perfect_for_tags: Date Night, Drinking Good Cocktails, Bar

review: Janitor’s Closet is a microbar with great cocktails located in the basement of the FieldHouse Jones hotel in River North. It’s also literally in a former janitor’s closet, hidden behind a door that says “employees only” and decorated with hardware and cleaning supplies. Plan to make a reservation, and to play the free slot car racing available just down the hall on weekends.
perfect_for_tags: Date Night, Drinking Good Cocktails, Bar

review: This bar in Logan Square focuses on spirit-free and CBD-infused cocktails alongside its alcoholic drinks. But even if you’re not super into their specialty concoctions, the menu and space are fun and unique enough that you’ll probably still have a good time. Make sure to split an order of the goth bread.
perfect_for_tags: Date Night, Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinks & A Light Bite, Eating At The Bar, Bar Food, Bar

review: Royal Palms in Bucktown feels like the world’s most photogenic cruise ship in the best way possible. The shuffleboard courts are first come, first served and can get backed up on the weekends, but there’s enough room to drink comfortably and plenty of other games to keep you occupied. There’s also a food truck dock with a sliding garage door so you can place your order without going outside, and a rooftop patio with a bar, complimentary sunscreen, and a winner-stays-on shuffleboard court.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Day Drinking, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar

review: The Bamboo Room is a secluded bar-within-a-bar at Three Dots And A Dash that’s much less busy than the main room. The staff has more time and energy to devote to serving you, and with a reservation you can experience a guided rum tasting with some of the most knowledgeable bartenders in the city.
perfect_for_tags: Birthdays, Date Night, Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinks & A Light Bite, Impressing Out of Towners, Special Occasions, Bar Food, Bar

review: District Brew Yards in West Town takes the pour-your-own-beer fad and transports it to a brewery taproom. It’s a collaboration between Twisted Hippo, Around The Bend Brew Co., Burnt City Brewing, Casa Humilde Cerveceria, and there are customer-operated taps for all four. It has a food hall vibe with big wooden tables that are perfect for getting work done or playing a board game with friends, and the huge windows that open up onto Ashland keep it from feeling too industrial. There’s also a BBQ from Lillie's Q, so there’s really no excuse to leave until they close.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Day Drinking, Brewery, BBQ

review: Primo Chuki’s is a popular spot on the border of Ravenswood and Uptown. This place is good for both carrying out and dining in, thanks to its large, airy dining room that’s great for groups. We’re big fans of the spicy and tender al pastor. It’s well seasoned, crispy, and juicy. The flavor is so good it really doesn’t need any salsa (but we like to add it anyway). While you’re at it, get a carne asada taco, too.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Late Night Eats, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Mexican, Tacos

review: La Internacional is a grocery store in Back of the Yards, and the first thing you need to do here is head to the taqueria in the back. There’s a serious taco operation happening back there, with a team of people seasoning and cooking meat, then assembling tacos with military precision. All the tacos are delicious, from the carnitas to the perfectly seared carne asada, and brimming over with filling. You can get them to go, but our favorite way to eat them is at the counter.
perfect_for_tags: Serious Take-Out Operation, Tacos

review: El Rincon is a casual sit-down spot in Archer Heights, and there’s a 90% chance that you’ll see parents eating with kids in soccer uniforms while you’re here. It’s a likable, family-friendly place with a short list of tacos on its menu. Our favorites are the chorizo (crispy, with a great amount of spice), arrachera (skirt steak), and cecina (dried beef or pork). While everything is well-prepared and delicious, it’s the green salsa that stands out here. The flavors are deep and spicy, which complements the rich meat perfectly.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Kids, Lunch, Walk-Ins, Mexican, Tacos

review: Casa Yari is a small Latin American BYOB restaurant in Logan Square with friendly service and excellent entrees, many of which can be made vegan or vegetarian using seitan or jackfruit as a meat substitute. We suggest ordering one of the mofongos - garlicky mountains of mashed plantains - and then finishing the meal with their flan, also available as a vegan option.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Quiet Meals, Vegans, Vegetarians, Walk-Ins, Latin

review: Miss Saigon is one of a few BYOB places along this stretch of restaurants on Argyle in Uptown. It’s not the most atmospheric, but choose Miss Saigon for the mi kho (brothless pho) served with crispy bone-in chicken. And definitely order the chicken wings, which are popular enough that the restaurant opened a satellite location focused solely on them.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Quiet Meals, Walk-Ins, Vietnamese, Southeast Asian

review: Goree is a great Senegalese restaurant on the border of Kenwood and Hyde Park. At lunch you can order one of their fantastic stews (our favorite is the maffe made with lamb, peanut butter, and yucca), and their entrees (like grilled red snapper or dibi chicken) are available all day. Portions are large, so come with a group and plan on sharing everything.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Senegalese

review: B’Gabs is a vegan cafe in Hyde Park that's open for breakfast and lunch, and almost everything here is made in house. The menu has lots of fruits and vegetables along with plenty of gluten-free and raw options. This is where you come for the type of food that will make you feel good about your healthy decisions - things like smoothie bowls, breakfast scrambles made with chickpeas, and a zucchini noodle pad thai salad. Everything tastes light and fresh, and if you’re a University of Chicago student with parents in town, it’s a great way to show them that living here doesn’t mean a steady diet of pizza, hot dogs, and Italian beef (though balance is important).
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Keeping It Kind Of Healthy, Lunch, Vegetarian, Vegan

review: At Millie’s you’re in for a lot of butter and a lot of kitsch. Modeled after supper clubs in the Northwoods of Wisconsin, the dining room is filled with vintage beer signs and taxidermy. Most entrees are just fine, but the Genuine Broaster Chicken is delicious - if you can catch the kitchen on a good night. Come here if you really miss Wisconsin but don’t feel like driving an hour to the border.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Walk-Ins, American

review: Considering how creative Marz’s beers and label art are, it’s not surprising that the Bridgeport taproom has the same artistic energy. It’s got everything you could want in a brewery taproom: a long wraparound bar, views of the production process, quirky party games, and even a small arcade room. The food menu is dominated by sandwiches, but it also offers snacks like giardiniera cheese dip and Sichuan beef jerky chips, and they serve brunch on the weekends.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Day Drinking, Eating At The Bar, Walk-Ins, Bar Food, Sandwiches

review: Bienmesabe is a casual BYOB Venezuelan restaurant in Ravenswood specializing in arepas. The value move here is to order arepas as your entree—we prefer the After Party (roasted pork, gouda cheese, and avocado slices). The pabellon (shredded flank steak over sweet plantains and rice) is also a standout, and the Bienmesabe Sampler is a heavy but tasty appetizer to share. Head to this spot if you’re already in the area with a bottle of wine and a gluten-free friend.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Gluten-Free Options, Vegans, Vegetarians, Venezuelan

review: Floriole is a bakery and cafe in Lincoln park that has delicious baked goods and pastries. Whether you need a cup of coffee and a croissant in the morning, a simple sandwich for lunch (like the B. A. D. - bacon, arugula, and date, which is incredible), or a few chocolate chip cookies in the afternoon because your sweet tooth is out of control, this is the spot.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Coffee & A Light Bite, French, Sandwiches

review: Caffe Oliva is a respectable outdoor restaurant on Ohio St. Beach. It’s kind of like ordering food at a hotel pool, with options like calamari, coconut shrimp, and pita and hummus. Are you going to call all your friends after eating here to tell them about the food? Probably not, but it gets the job done when you don’t feel like moving farther from the sand than absolutely necessary.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Lunch, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American, Bar Food

review: There are a few La Michoacanas in Chicago, and the one we really like is in Pilsen. It has a drive-thru, the people are friendly, and they have great paletas and scoops of ice cream. The treats here are very sweet, perfect for when you want a dessert that tastes like dessert, because not everyone wants an abundance of goat cheese or matcha. Our favorite is the cajeta ice cream, which tastes like frozen condensed milk in the best way, and the rice pudding cream paleta, which is milky and sweet with little bits of rice in it that we really like.
perfect_for_tags: Kids, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Mexican, Ice Cream
full_address: 1855 S Blue Island Ave, Chicago, IL 60608

review: This is a Japanese soft serve shop in Wicker Park with only two flavors to choose from: matcha and sesame. The soft serve here is perfectly creamy, and both varieties are well balanced. The best thing to do is order the Rakki Royale, a swirl of both that comes with red beans, white mochi, coffee jelly, chestnut, rice puffs, sesame brittle, and a piece of matcha cheesecake. It’s not too sweet, has a lot of different textures, and is something you need to have.
perfect_for_tags: Cheap Eats, Quick Eats, Walk-Ins, Japanese

review: Raised is a cute flower-box-lined rooftop right on Wacker and State with a great view of the Chicago River. This spot is low key, with a menu of elevated bar food items like tenderloin sliders, lobster rolls, and charcuterie that’s good for sharing. Come here when you don’t want to worry about being blown away by gale force winds.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinks & A Light Bite, Impressing Out of Towners, Outdoor/Patio Situation, People Watching, American, Bar Food
full_address: 1 West Upper Wacker Drive, Chicago, IL 60601

review: There aren’t a lot of upscale spots near McCormick Place worth spending time at. Vu is a rooftop bar on the 22nd floor of a nearby building, and since it has both firepits and retractable windows it’s good for the occasional April snowstorm and/or autumn. There’s a long menu of small plates, with dishes like mushroom tostadas, chorizo and shrimp toast, and steak tartare. It’s all fine, but our favorite activity here is to drink and wonder how the Morningstar Investment Conference is going.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Drinking Good Cocktails, Impressing Out of Towners, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American, Bar Food

review: Flo & Santos is part Polish-American restaurant, part pizza spot in the South Loop. The pies here are tavern-style thin crust, and you can also get things like pierogis. It’s a short walk from Museum Campus and has a little patio that’s nice in the summertime.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Day Drinking, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American, Pizza

review: If you haven’t gone to Shawn Michelle’s in Bronzeville, that needs to change immediately. This place makes fantastic ice cream, with creative flavors that are interesting without seeming like they’re trying too hard. Order the honey cinnamon graham cracker (which has a perfect balance of crackers and honey), the rich and smooth banana pudding, or the Delta, which tastes like an oddly satisfying creamy Kool-aid. If you’re a first-timer, expect to be practically force-fed samples of their signature flavors by the friendliest people who seem like the only thing they care about in this world is for you to like their ice cream - which you will.
perfect_for_tags: Quick Eats, Walk-Ins, Ice Cream

review: It’s hard to remember there was a time when Chicago didn’t have 75,894 Lettuce Entertain You restaurants. But before them all was RJ Grunts in Lincoln Park. The food at RJs is American and probably won’t blow you away, but if you’re with family and want to go somewhere kid-friendly with a good burger and a salad bar with more than 50 ingredients (that’s not an exaggeration), come here.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Classic Establishment, Kids, Literally Everyone, Strollers, American
full_address: 2056 N. Lincoln Park W., Chicago, IL 60614

review: The Budlong Hot Chicken has a few locations in the city, including this one on Armitage, which you should stop into if you’re looking for a solid counter service option in Lincoln Park. You can get a boneless chicken sandwich or chicken tenders with plenty of a la carte sides to choose from, or you can get the bone-in hot chicken plate with toast and pickles, which we recommend.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, American, Southern

review: As hard as we try to pretend it is, Lake Michigan is not an ocean. That said, there are some spots along the “beach” that manage to convince you that you’re closer to the Jersey Shore than to Gary, Indiana. The Dock at Montrose Beach in Uptown achieves this - it’s a cafe right on the lakefront sand. And while the burger might be mediocre, the convenience definitely isn’t.
perfect_for_tags: Live Music, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American
full_address: 200 W Montrose Harbor Dr, Chicago, IL 60640

review: Waterfront Cafe is attached to a coach house next to the Berger Park Cultural Center mansion in Edgewater. It’s quiet and has food like nachos, red pepper spread, and sandwiches. There’s also live acoustic music. It’s basically the beach restaurant equivalent of linen pants, and a great alternative to the scenier lake spots in the city,
perfect_for_tags: Lunch, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Live Music, American

review: If you’ve always wondered what’s up with that giant boat on North Avenue Beach, it’s Castaways. And while this place is a total sh*tshow, if you want a burger after drinking at the beach all day and/or love hearing radio DJs broadcast Top 40 hits, then this is the place to be - provided you’re in party mode.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Outdoor/Patio Situation, People Watching, Bar Food
full_address: 1603 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60614

review: If you don’t have a beach vacation in your future, Shore Club can help. This place on North Avenue Beach has a cabana-style atmosphere with loungy daybeds and some not-terrible Mediterranean food. And unlike an ocean beach, you won’t need to worry about sharks. Probably.
perfect_for_tags: Outdoor/Patio Situation, Mediterranean

review: Flat & Point is a grill-focused spot in Logan Square. It specializes in wood-fired meat, and it has a short rotating menu. You’ll find dishes like wagyu brisket, porchetta, and pork belly mac and cheese. The menu is constantly changing, so just be aware that it’s the kind of spot where they might change a dish between the time you sit down and when you actually order. But whatever is on offer, you can count on the meat to be perfectly cooked, and everything (the bread, the pasta, the tables - yes, we’re serious) to be made in house.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Walk-Ins, American, BBQ

review: 5 Loaves Eatery is a casual breakfast spot on the South Side specializing in Southern and soul food. You can get delicious dishes like fried chicken with pancakes or waffles, fluffy omelets with grits, and things that you could make yourself (like a bacon, egg, and cheese sandwich on toast), but won’t involve cleaning bacon splatter off your stove. 5 Loaves is small and can get crowded, but the friendly service and great food will make the wait worth it.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Coffee & A Light Bite, Walk-Ins, American, Southern

review: Pearl’s Place in Bronzeville focuses on Southern food, serving breakfast all day in a space that looks like a mid-range hotel’s nondescript dining room. There’s a regular menu with things like omelets and pancakes, but the best way to eat here is by going full-on breakfast buffet, which is available every day. And that’s where you’ll also find pancakes, grits, breakfast meats, an omelet bar, and chicken wings - basically anything you can think of, and some stuff you might not, like salmon croquettes. It’s affordable (the buffet is $12.99), and enjoying as much of it as possible is a justifiable reason for being late to work.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Breakfast, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Classic Establishment, Dinner with the Parents, Lunch, Southern

review: This is an old-school neighborhood dive bar in Pilsen with great burgers, cheap beer, crispy tater tots, and live music on Monday nights. You can’t go wrong with a quick drink and a casual dinner here.
perfect_for_tags: Happy Hour, Bar Food

review: Tack Room is a piano bar attached to Thalia Hall, in what used to be an old-timey carriage house. These days, instead of coming here to saddle your horse, you come to drink cocktails and listen to live music in a dimly-lit space filled with candles.
perfect_for_tags: Date Night, Drinking Good Cocktails, Bar

review: Canton Regio is a Mexican restaurant in Pilsen. This place looks like a cross between a rustic Southwestern barn and an old church - all brick and wood, with incredibly high vaulted ceilings and things like saddles and wagon wheels on the wall. The service is really friendly, and the menu focuses on grilled meat, which means you can share things like incredibly tender steaks, brochetas with shrimp or chicken served dangling from medieval-looking hooks, and fajitas. Everything is well-seasoned and perfectly cooked, and this place also makes its own flour tortillas - which are so good we’d consider coming here just to eat those.
perfect_for_tags: Mexican

review: Da Mao Jia is a small Chinese restaurant in a strip mall in an industrial section of Bridgeport. The food is Sichuan, with a short menu of tender braised dishes (like ribs and duck tongue), barbecue (including some fantastic pulled rabbit), and small plates like the sweet and spicy handmade noodles and bell dumplings, both of which have a great amount of heat. While the space gets crowded, it’s still typically pretty easy to get a table here. Come with one or two friends (or by yourself) when you’re looking for a quick and delicious meal.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Dining Solo, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Small Plates, Chinese

review: Twisted Hippo is a brew pub in Albany Park with bright colors, some arcade games, and pink cartoon hippos decorating the walls. The food menu is pretty standard, with mac and cheese, burgers, and fried things like corn dogs and cheese curds, and all of these things are better-than-average bar bites. And while prices seem high at first (a corn dog with fries costs $13), everything listed on the menu includes tax and tip.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Eating At The Bar, Kids, American, Bar Food

review: Margie’s has been around since 1921, and looks like it. This is the kind of place where an adult can order the “World’s Largest Terrapin” - a sundae with 15 scoops of ice cream - and not feel judged. Eat your giant sundae in a clamshell bowl with gravy boats of homemade hot fudge and caramel on the side, or take said sundae to-go when it’s too nice to sit inside somewhere, no matter how charming that place is.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Breakfast, Classic Establishment, Impressing Out of Towners, Kids, Literally Everyone, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Strollers, Walk-Ins, American, Bakery/Cafe

review: The name and concept of Table, Donkey and Stick is a nod to the eating and drinking traditions of the Alps—specifically, the idea that people need a warm place to escape the cold. Think Midwest version of a Bavarian Inn, with hearty comfort foods like charcuterie, smoked beef heart, and confit duck leg. Come here to sit at the bar with an Old Fashioned, and eat something that will sustain you till May.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinking Good Wine, Quiet Meals, Small Plates, German, Eastern European

review: Aurelio’s is a South Side pizza chain that’s been around since 1959. The specialty here is tavern-style thin crust pizza (the kind that’s cut into little squares), and it’s greasy in a good way, and great to eat with beer. The old-school-pizza-parlor-style space is perfect for large groups, so grab some friends, order a few pitchers, and start arguing over those weird middle pieces.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Day Drinking, Kids, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Strollers, Bar Food, Pizza

review: This isn’t remarkable pizza, but it is drunk food at its finest. Big G’s in Wrigleyville serves kind-of-weird-but-actually-pretty-good slices that sound like they were made using a Chopped basket, with toppings like BBQ beef and french fries, s’mores, and mac and cheese. If you’ve never had mac and cheese on a pizza, this must be your first time in the Midwest. Welcome.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Delivery, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Pizza

review: There are now Shake Shacks all over Chicago. And one popped up in Wrigleyville before you even had time to grieve the loss of the Taco Bell that was torn down. Let this place console you with tasty burgers, and a specialty concrete made with frozen custard and a seasonal slice of Bang Bang Pie.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Late Night Eats, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, American, Burgers

review: Old Town Pour House is a large sports bar in Old Town. High ceilings allow for a couple of huge TV’s, and the slightly upscale nature of the bar means quality food as well. Any of the sandwiches or burgers are a good way to go, and pair them with one of the seemingly endless amount of beers Pour House has on tap.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Day Drinking, Drinking Good Cocktails, Sports!, Bar Food

review: Since Ranalli’s was revamped a few years ago it’s become an excellent environment to watch a game. The patio is ideal in the summer, but the influx of TV’s, quality pizzas, and other bar food will always treat you well. The convenient Lincoln Park location is also a strong bargaining chip if you have friends that live all over the city.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Serious Take-Out Operation, Sports!, Pizza

review: Roost is one of our favorite spots in Chicago for fried chicken sandwiches, and we’re happy there’s an outpost in Wrigleyville. It’s a small counter-service operation, and the menu here has the same fantastic fried chicken sandwiches and biscuits that you’ll find in other locations. They have four varieties, including the house style (with pickles, coleslaw, and chipotle ranch) and the sunrise (with egg, bacon, and cheddar). You’ll get a choice of brioche or biscuit, and you should go with a biscuit - unless you get one of each.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, American, Sandwiches

review: Like the Do-Rite locations in Streeterville and the West Loop, the Wrigleyville location has fried chicken sandwiches as well as delicious donuts, including some vegan and gluten-free options. They serve tasty breakfast sandwiches (on buns or donuts), too, if for some reason you’re wandering around Wrigleyville in the morning.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Coffee & A Light Bite, Gluten-Free Options, Serious Take-Out Operation, Vegans, Vegetarians, American, Sandwiches

review: Smoke Daddy is a very large, very bright BBQ spot in Wrigleyville that kind of feels like a chain restaurant, even though there’s only one other location (in Wicker Park). This one is on the same block as the Hotel Zachary, and has an upstairs patio along with enough TVs to make it basically qualify as a sports bar. Does it serve the best BBQ in the city? No. But the food here is pretty tasty, and there’s live music seven days a week. Get a sampler platter, plus some cornbread and baked beans.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Day Drinking, Kids, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Sports!, BBQ

review: This is a small counter-service operation with delicious baked empanadas. They have about 15 varieties daily, with flavors like beef, Nutella and banana, or bacon with date and goat cheese. They’re all really good, and the best strategy is to order as many as can fit on your table.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Dining Solo, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Vegetarians, Walk-Ins, Latin, Argentinian

review: Molly's Cupcakes is a bakery in Lincoln Park that specializes in filled cupcakes that seem like they were designed by an eight-year-old. This means you'll find options stuffed with cake batter, Nutella, or cookie dough. Whatever you get you can expect them to be very sweet, rich, and delicious.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Bakery/Cafe

review: The original location of this old-school Chinese bakery is in Chinatown, and we’re really glad there’s one on the North Side. Chiu Quon is fantastic, and you can’t go wrong with anything from their pastry case. They have incredible pork buns, sponge cakes, sesame balls, egg custards, and much more. Everything is made fresh daily, and there are plenty of tables inside, too. Just plan ahead - it’s cash-only.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Cheap Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Walk-Ins, Chinese, Bakery/Cafe

review: This is the the second location of Beatnik, and as the name suggests, it is indeed on the river. There’s outdoor seating, and like its sister restaurant in West Town it’s decorated with ornate touches and plants that have a tropical feel. It also serves the same style of Mediterranean food and cocktails.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinks & A Light Bite, First/Early in the Game Dates, Impressing Out of Towners, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Small Plates, Vegetarians, Mediterranean

review: Roots is a solid neighborhood option for dine-in pizza in West Town. The pies are Quad Cities-style, which means they’re round but cut into rectangles, and the toppings are under the cheese. The menu is huge, with a decent selection of salads and rotating roster of pizzas designed by local chefs. A huge bar area and large patio, as well as the interesting specialty pies, make it a great local spot for a hangout - especially if you’re with a large group.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Day Drinking, Delivery, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Pizza

review: Urban Vegan is a vegan Thai restaurant in Ravenswood. It used to mainly be a carryout spot, but now it’s a full sit-down restaurant. You’ll find dishes like tofu satay, soy chicken with peanut sauce, and a number of curries. It’s a fantastic neighborhood option for vegan Asian food.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Keeping It Kind Of Healthy, Serious Take-Out Operation, Vegans, Vegetarians, Vegetarian

review: Ignotz is a very good Italian restaurant in a pocket neighborhood inside Pilsen called the Heart Of Chicago. The chicken parmigiana is worth traveling for, and the lasagna is really good, too. Not to mention that they win the award for best table bread setup, since it comes with a roasted bulb of garlic for spreading, plus some breadsticks you’ll only wish were unlimited. The whole restaurant is in a refurbished house, and you’ll be eating in a living room complete with a fireplace, and family photos on the mantel.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Dinner with the Parents, Drinking Good Wine, Kids, Italian

review: Club Lucky is an Italian restaurant in Bucktown that's meant to resemble an old 1940s Italian supper club. It’s loud and crowded and the main dining room is huge, with lots of tables and big leather booths. Come here with a group, and prepare to float away on a sea of martinis and red sauce. Order the fantastic handmade cavatelli in vodka sauce, and you can’t go wrong with the lightly fried calamari as an appetizer. Most of the dishes here are meant to serve two, so we mean it when we say you should come here with friends.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Classic Establishment, Date Night, Dinner with the Parents, Drinking Good Cocktails, People Watching, Italian
full_address: 1824 W Wabansia Ave, Bucktown/Wicker Park, IL 60622

review: This Lincoln Park Italian restaurant is popular for a reason - it has great pastas and attentive service. The three dining rooms (on two levels) are always really busy, so you should definitely make a reservation. The bread here is delicious, and so are all the sauces - order the bolognese with housemade rigatoni, or go with their gnocchi in a pesto sauce.
perfect_for_tags: Birthdays, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Dinner with the Parents, Drinking Good Wine, First/Early in the Game Dates, Italian

review: Mart Anthony’s is an out-of-the way spot on the border of West Town and the West Loop. It looks like a typical neighborhood corner bar, because, well, it is. But it also happens to be a pretty great Italian restaurant. On any given night it’s full of friends getting together after work, and couples on casual dates. The servers and bartenders are warm and welcoming, and will chat with you even if you’re not a regular. Get the braciole or the lasagna, both of which will have you covered in the leftover department for about three days. All the sauces here are very flavorful, and the housemade sausage is particularly good.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Business Meals, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Drinking Good Cocktails, Drinking Good Wine, Eating At The Bar, First/Early in the Game Dates, Happy Hour, Italian

review: Riccardo Enoteca is a casual Italian spot in Lincoln Park. The focus here is on antipasti, pastas, and pizzas, and if you’re looking for a low-key meal, this is a great option. It’s small and usually crowded, and a good choice if you happen to have small children with you.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Dinner with the Parents, Drinking Good Wine, Eating At The Bar, First/Early in the Game Dates, Kids, Italian

review: The West Loop isn’t known for having an abundance of quiet, old-school spots. In fact, nowadays most of Restaurant Row is full of trendy new places, fast-casual chain restaurants, and the McDonalds that takes up half a block. Head to Viaggio when you want to keep it simple with a neighborhood institution. It’s been around for more than 10 years (which is about 50 in West Loop years), and the food is exactly what you want it to be: tasty and comforting. Get the meatball salad. Yes, you read that correctly.
perfect_for_tags: Business Meals, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Dinner with the Parents, First/Early in the Game Dates, Quiet Meals, Italian

review: Reggies is a casual venue on the Near South Side that has live music, open mic comedy nights, and karaoke. It also has a great rooftop, which makes it ideal for a group hang in the summer. Especially if you’re more interested in beer, bar food, and getting loud than appreciating the view of State Street.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Dancing, Day Drinking, Eating At The Bar, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar Food

review: Moneygun is a very fun bar that’s attached to Saint Lou’s Assembly in the West Loop. It has big leather booths, great music, and old-school drinks like White Russians, negronis, and daiquiris. Come here after dinner next door, and plan to hang all night.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Bar Food

review: The J. Parker in the Hotel Lincoln is a covered rooftop bar that’s completely encased in glass, giving you a 360-degree view of city, and probably even some vitamin D. Come here with out-of-towners to show off the city, and grab some drinks before heading out for the night.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Drinks & A Light Bite, Impressing Out of Towners, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar Food
full_address: 1816 N Clark St Fl 13, Chicago, IL 60614

review: The taproom of Half Acre Beer Company is a very comfortable and relaxing spot to spend the day. Plus, they have a short food menu consisting primarily of some very good burritos. When you find yourself Googling homebrew recipes instead of finishing that PowerPoint presentation, you might want to switch to coffee - which, conveniently, they also serve.
perfect_for_tags: Day Drinking, Delivery, Drinks & A Light Bite, Bar Food

review: Noon O Kabab is a Persian restaurant in Albany Park with a really long menu of dishes perfect for sharing with friends. Like the adass polo (seasoned rice made with caramelized onions), and all of the kebabs. There are two dining areas—one that's more upscale, and one that’s casual and focused on carry-out. So it's great whether we want a nicer sit-down dinner or want to eat kabobs on the couch while having a Netflix marathon.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Serious Take-Out Operation, Middle Eastern

review: Izakaya is the very dark bar that's located in the basement of Momotaro in the West Loop. Come here for drinks and great Japanese small plates (like don buri and a burger made with house made bao) that you can't find upstairs. It's a great low-key option in the neighborhood.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Eating At The Bar, First/Early in the Game Dates, Small Plates, Japanese, Sushi

review: Paradise Park is the third restaurant from the same people who have Homeslice and Happy Camper. Like those places, it has satisfying dorm-room-style pies and an over-the-top atmosphere. The theme here is “kitschy trailer park,” with flamingo lawn ornaments, swing sets, and a Winnebago out on the patio.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Pizza

review: Rick Bayless is such a famous Chicago chef that he has his own urban legends:  When Rick Bayless chops onions the onions cry. Rick Bayless can put a kitchen fire out with gasoline. If it looks like chicken, tastes like chicken, and feels like chicken, but Rick Bayless says it’s beef, then it’s beef. You get the point. Topolobampo is Rick’s Mexican restaurant in River North that serves three different seasonal tasting menus (starting at $95 and going to $140), and the food is so good, it will remind you why he has his own holiday - OK, we made that up.
perfect_for_tags: Special Occasions, Mexican

review: Chicago loves putting restaurants in alleys. Maybe because (unlike New York, where garbage is proudly displayed on the street) we just have so many of them. Bar Sotano is a cocktail bar in the alley behind Frontera Grill, and it’s owned by the same team. So it’s not surprising that the Mexican food here is great. The menu has a mix of bar snacks (like habanero-glazed fried chicken bites), plus entrees like a burger and a wagyu steak with pureed sunchoke. Which is probably one of the best steaks you’ll have the chance to eat in an alley.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Eating At The Bar, Mexican

review: The West Loop can be overwhelming, with lots of crowded places full of people who seem like their entire lives are hinging on the amount of fun they’re having tonight. This is not the case at Eleven Eleven, an upscale spot that’s relatively relaxed. They have a long wine list, and (if you want) the bartenders will talk to you extensively about the the selection. But there’s also a very good food menu, with options like lamb sausage stuffed peppers, cheese and charcuterie, and a collard green grilled cheese that tastes like something your stoner roommate who’s also a very good chef would make after a night out.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Wine Bar

review: Want to go all out? Pops For Champagne in River North is the move. It's a wine bar with a large menu of sparkling wine, champagne, and champagne cocktails. On the food side of things, there’s a bunch of cheeses and charcuterie, and plenty of caviar. If you’re having a night out and feel like going for broke, this place will definitely impress your friends.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Wine Bar

review: Ward Eight is on the border of Chicago and Evanston, and it’s a great, not-too-well-known option if you’re getting together with your friends who live up north. It feels a little like a dive bar, but it’s too clean to actually be a dive. Inside it’s dark and small, with wooden floors and walls, and reclaimed church pews for seats. Cocktails are straightforward, and the drink menu focuses on excellent renditions of the classics, like Old Fashioneds. Food-wise, you’ll find charcuterie and sandwiches, as well as a fantastic chocolate cake that’s good enough to make the drinks the afterthought.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Bar Food

review: It’s not quite clear at what point we decided to charge more money for food courts and call them “food halls,” but it probably doesn’t matter, since generally speaking, food halls seem to have better food. That’s definitely the case at Aster Hall, a new food hall inside the 900 N. Michigan building. It’s from the same group that owns Au Cheval, and it has 16 different places to eat and drink, including outposts of 3 Greens Market, Green Street Smoked Meats, and Small Cheval. The food is high-quality and reasonably priced - which is useful, because if you’re in this neighborhood, you’re probably spending a lot of money on something already. As a bonus, the upstairs area has a very nice view and is great for getting some work done.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Lunch, American, Burgers

review: Bars that serve good food are a wonderful thing, and that’s why we really like Tricycle in Wicker Park. This spot definitely feels more like a Chicago bar than a restaurant, mainly because the bar itself dominates the space. But it also has a long food menu with a wide range of options that taste really good. You’ll find bacon-wrapped dates, roasted cauliflower with a fantastic curry sauce, and a deconstructed chicken pot pie. In other words, this place is a good reason to hit up a neighborhood bar for dinner.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, American, Bar Food

review: Before Sushi Mike opened the new fancy digs in the West Loop, there was the original in  Andersonville. This location has the same quality sushi, just in a more laid-back environment. So come here for sushi that’s good and reasonably priced. Tanoshii is perfect for a weekday dinner or low-key date night.
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Sushi

review: Nookies is a Chicago diner staple (the Old Town location as been around since 1973) for a casual breakfast, lunch, or dinner. This place has a lengthy menu that rivals the Cheesecake Factory’s, so you can eat everything from eggs and potatoes to meatloaf, and every location except the one in Edgewater is BYOB. That said, we prefer Nookies for brunch - and we particularly like the crunchy French toast, battered and fried in corn flakes.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, BYOB, American

review: Lincoln Park is full of casual spots that are affordable enough for college students, and Toro falls into this category - helped along by the fact that it’s BYOB.  Because of its high quality sushi, small space, and no-reservations policy, this place is always crowded. Increase your chances of getting a table by coming with just one other person, not a group. But you should still expect a wait (and to be surrounded by college students).
perfect_for_tags: BYOB, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Japanese, Sushi

review: Dog Haus is a hot dog chain from LA that was brave enough to open a location in a city that’s highly opinionated about hot dogs. It was a good decision - the hot dogs here are really good, in part because all of them are served on King’s Hawaiian buns. The specialty versions, in particular, are delicious - we especially like the Scott Baioli (with caramelized onions) - and the drinks are highly affordable. The space is large, making this a good place for big groups of people looking to not spend a ton of money. They even have an off-menu Chicago-style dog you can order.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Eating At The Bar, Bar Food, Hot Dogs

review: M. Henry is a great weekday breakfast spot in Andersonville. This BYOB restaurant has everything from bacon-wrapped baked eggs to fluffy pancakes covered in blueberries and granola. Unsurprisingly, it’s usually crowded on the weekends, so expect a wait.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Lunch, Bakery/Cafe, Breakfast

review: This Wicker Park cocktail spot is hidden behind a little record shop (called, straightforwardly, The Record Shop) - and while you can actually buy records there if you want, you should go in and tell them you’re looking for Dorian’s. They’ll let you into the bar at the back, where the atmosphere is loud and fun. There are plenty of tables and comfy seats, and the short food menu has a collection of great Asian and Indian small plates, like a short rib banh mi and a delicious pork belly larb. This is the kind of place where you can easily end up spending your entire night, whether you meant to or not.
perfect_for_tags: Drinks & A Light Bite, Small Plates, Indian, Southeast Asian

review: There are only a few good drinks-and-a-light-bite options in the neighborhood, and Two Lights is one of them. It’s right across the street from Second City, and inside it looks kind of like an upscale seafood shack, with a long bar that works well for small groups or dining solo. The menu involves mainly seafood-focused small plates, and you should stick with dishes like the tuna poke tacos, shrimp, and oysters, all of which are good.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Pre-Theater Eats, American, Seafood

review: As the name suggests, this place has a theme: it’s decorated like a cabin from the 1800s. In keeping with that idea, there’s a lot of game on the menu. For a celebration, consider arranging one of their whole animal meals - you can choose from things like antelope leg, alligator, or wild boar. And there’s a lot of space outside, making it great for a big group hang outdoors.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Unique Dining Experience, American

review: RM Champagne is a romantic wine bar in the West Loop. It’s the perfect solution for a romantic date night when you can’t decide whether to take someone out for dinner or drinks. Settle in over a cocktail on their twinkly light patio out back, or order small bites oysters and crab claws if things are going well.
perfect_for_tags: Date Night, Drinks & A Light Bite, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Wine Bar

review: Reno is leading a double life. Come in the morning for homemade bagels and delicious breakfast sandwiches, or at night for interesting pizzas, like one topped with pork belly carnitas, salsa verde, mozzarella, and cotija cheese. It doesn’t matter to us which of these is the “real” Reno - we like them both.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Pizza, Bagels

review: The Gage is our top choice in the Loop for bar food. The menu is full of elevated classics, like bison tartare, poutine, and entrees like fish and chips. Since this spot is right across from Millenium Park, you can also plan on it being full of tourists. But at least they’re the cool kind of tourists who know where to go for a good meal.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Lunch, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Bar Food, Gastropub

review: This Andersonville shop sells lots of sugary things - like candy, baked goods, and, of course, ice cream. The ice cream they serve is from Chocolate Shoppe, a Wisconsin brand, and you’ll find 32 flavors that rotate regularly (including sugar-free and dairy-free options). The ice cream alone is good, but we like coming here for sundaes in particular. They make sure to put hot fudge on the inside of the cup as well on top, which means you get plenty in each bite. This place is always packed, so get your sundae and walk around all the neighborhood shops.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Bakery/Cafe

review: The emphasis at Hoosier Mama in Evanston is on pie, and you shouldn’t come here without getting at least one piece, although you’ll probably be tempted to leave with five. They’re all exceptionally good, from chocolate cream to whatever fruit options they have that day. There are also delicious savory options, like quiche, sandwiches, and salads. Come here to get some work done in the natural-light-filled space, or just to catch up with friends. And pie. You definitely need to catch up with pie.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Serious Take-Out Operation, Bakery/Cafe

review: Eating at Found in Evanston is like hanging out in a funky but nice furniture store. Meaning it’s full of mismatched chairs and tables, table lamps, and desks decorated with vases. The menu is also eclectic, with food ranging from stinging nettle flatbreads to caviar, but the food is solid, and this place is a great option for a low-key dinner (or just drinks and some appetizers). Definitely check it out if you want nothing more than to eat and drink in a living room without worrying about using coasters.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Date Night, Drinks & A Light Bite, Outdoor/Patio Situation, American

review: This is a bar in Evanston with a menu of bar food and sausages (with options like duck sausage and a crawfish andouille). It’s decorated like a British pub/upscale hunting lodge, and it’s a good place to get drinks and/or talk about your thesis over some bratwurst.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Eating At The Bar, Bar Food, Burgers

review: This is a bakery in Evanston that makes some truly wonderful bread (with loaves like a pumpkin seed with rosemary, and caramelized onion rye), plus pastries like croissants and kouign-amann. But they also have a small selection of excellent sandwiches and flatbreads. It’s a great place to pick up some stuff for a picnic, even if your “picnic” involves you eating a baguette alone in your car.
perfect_for_tags: Coffee & A Light Bite, Serious Take-Out Operation, Bakery/Cafe

review: Peckish Pig is a restuarant on the border of Evanston and Chicago. Come for bar snacks like bacon-fat popcorn, or plates like fish and chips and burgers. They have eight or so beers on tap, and they’re mainly IPAs that go well with the gastropub food. The space is crowded and lively, so it’s ideal for a group dinner or double date.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Gastropub

review: There’s a location of Union Squared in the Loop at Revival Food Hall, but the full-service restaurant version is in Evanston. The specialty here is Detroit-style pizza, which is basically a hybrid of the pan-style you get at Pequod’s and the deep dish from Lou Malnati’s (so it has a caramelized crust and sauce on top - the best of both worlds). There’s not a ton of space, but tables turn over quickly, and in the summer you can sit on the back patio.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Serious Take-Out Operation, Pizza

review: Edzo’s is an old-school burger joint in Evanston, serving fantastic griddled diner-style patties, hot dogs, and fries. The orange, yellow, and brown color scheme reminds us of a puffy jacket from the 1980s, but it just adds to the retro charm of the place. Make sure to get an order of their specialty fries (like buffalo with bleu cheese, or the chili fries) and an Oreo shake.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Classic Establishment, Lunch, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, American, Burgers

review: Food at college bars frequently tastes like it came from the freezer section at Costco. So we get excited when we find a spot that has great, fresh-tasting stuff, and that’s why we really like Bat 17 in Evanston. The menu has the usual suspects, like burgers, sandwiches, and fries, but they’re made with high-quality ingredients (like, in some cases, housemade bread). The space is full of TVs, pool tables, and foosball, and while it definitely feels like a college hangout, you’re welcome even if you’ve paid off all your loans (or have been deferring for a few years now).
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, American, Bar Food

review: Tomate Fresh Kitchen is a small carry-out spot in Evanston that got its start selling Latin American food at the farmers’ market. They have tasty burritos, gorditos, and tacos, including interesting vegetarian options like sweet potato with caramelized onion, and yucca chimichurri. Whatever you order, you can count on it being fantastic. In fact, the only problem with this place is that it isn’t open later - they close at 6pm.
perfect_for_tags: Casual Weeknight Dinner, Cheap Eats, Lunch, Quick Eats, Serious Take-Out Operation, Latin, Vegetarian

review: Taco Diablo is the Evanston equivalent of Big Star, but with no patio and better food. The menu is short, and mainly consists of 12 types of tacos - including lamb barbacoa, a chorizo made from duck and pork, and classics like carne asada. They’re all delicious, and they come come three to an order (you can mix and match) with family-style beans and rice for the table. The dark cantina-like space has a large bar and plenty of booths for big groups. Come here with friends and find a way to try every single taco on the menu.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Day Drinking, Eating At The Bar, Literally Everyone, Mexican, Tacos

review: Cochon Volant is underneath a Hyatt hotel in the Loop. This spot is designed to feel like a French brasserie, with vintage-looking marble tables, a bakery counter, and a menu full of French food. It does a good job of temporarily helping you forget that the neighboring stores include a Starbucks, Dunkin Donuts, Wendy’s, Noodles & Co., and McDonald’s. Get their cheeseburger royale - it’s excellent.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Outdoor/Patio Situation, Pre-Theater Eats, French

review: There are  a lot of great spots at the Chicago Athletic Association, like The Game Room (a cocktail bar) and Cherry Circle Room, an upscale restaurant on the second floor. The main design elements are dark wood, overstuffed leather chairs, and a huge fireplace. It reminds us of a fancy turn-of-the-century lodge, and the rustic menu (with plenty of roasted meat) fits the ambiance.
perfect_for_tags: Birthdays, Corporate Cards, Dinner with the Parents, Impressing Out of Towners, Pre-Theater Eats, American

review: The Dearborn is an easy-to-like spot in the Loop with a well-rounded American menu that works for a lot of occasions. It’s nice enough for a business dinner, but still casual enough for lunch after that Segway tour you took with your parents. Plus, the space is huge, with multiple rooms that work for large groups or couples on a date. Order the pork belly appetizer and any of the salads, then make sure someone gets a cheeseburger—it’s really good.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Business Meals, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Impressing Out of Towners, Pre-Theater Eats, Walk-Ins, American

review: 3 Squares is an upscale diner in Uptown with comfortable booths and a long counter that’s perfect for dining solo. You can get dishes like omelettes, chicken and waffles, and a Chicago pastrami “dog” (a pastrami sandwich dressed like a classic Chicago hot dog). Breakfast is served all day, so if you’re a breakfast-for-dinner person, you’ll be particularly happy here.
perfect_for_tags: Breakfast, Brunch, Casual Weeknight Dinner, American, Diner

review: This is a fancy spot at the top of The Peninsula, a luxury hotel near Michigan Ave. Because of its location, it has a great view of the Magnificent Mile, which makes it an ideal place to take out-of-towners. You’ll find small plates like foie gras-filled bon bons and marrow “poppers” (which are basically tater tots filled with bone marrow). Come here and eat some expensive bar food with anyone you’re trying impress.
perfect_for_tags: Corporate Cards, Day Drinking, Drinks & A Light Bite, Impressing Out of Towners, Bar Food

review: This is the Fish Bar at Navy Pier, and a good dining option when you're here. Order the shrimp and crawfish po’boy (it’s the same excellent sandwich that’s at the location in Lakeview), or the fried fish sandwich. And make sure you get a shake, too.
perfect_for_tags: Kids, Pre-Theater Eats, Strollers, Bar Food, Seafood

review: This Navy Pier outpost is an acceptable alternative to the Michigan Ave. location of Billy Goat Tavern. Whichever location you pick, make sure to order the double or the triple burger - the bun’s too thick for a single patty.
perfect_for_tags: Classic Establishment, American, Bar Food

review: Dutch & Docs, is an all-day brasserie in Wrigleyville from the same people who own the steakhouse Swift & Sons, and this place serves the same high-quality, well-prepared steaks as its sister restaurant. There are also housemade pastas (like pappardelle with beef and pork ragu) and bar snacks like fried giardiniera. It’s basically an upscale sports bar, and even has a view of the stadium. Come here on game days with a group, or for a casual weeknight dinner in Wrigleyville - something that until recently didn’t seem like a very good idea.
perfect_for_tags: Big Groups, Birthdays, Casual Weeknight Dinner, Dining Solo, Eating At The Bar, American, Bar Food

review: This is an eight-seat bar that’s also in the Chicago Athletic Association Hotel. You need to buy tickets for a seating here (they’re $50, but the price goes towards your drinks), and there’s a two-hour time limit on your seating. They serve cocktails (made with very rare vintage scotches and other spirits) omakase-style, and the bartender will tailor yours to your preferences.
perfect_for_tags: Corporate Cards, Date Night, Impressing Out of Towners, Special Occasions, Bar

review: The Violet Hour in Wicker Park is a good destination cocktail bar from the people who own Avec and The Publican. This place might seem like it’s trying hard to be cool - from the unmarked door to the “House Rules” (which ban baseball caps, Cosmopolitans, and any drink that’s a -bomb, jager or otherwise). It doesn’t come off as obnoxious, though, because the craft cocktails really are good. Inside, it feels like a lounge more than a bar - it’s dark, with lots of candlelight, plus comfy chairs and tables that can be sectioned off for privacy. Overall, not a bad spot to celebrate the launch of your top-secret baseball-cap-recycling startup.
perfect_for_tags: Corporate Cards, Date Night, Impressing Out of Towners, Special Occasions, Bar

review: Even though it’s well-known (especially as a spot for pre-wedding get-togethers), Drumbar still feels like nobody has discovered how nice it is.
